21.       The Committee strongly disapproves the procedure adopted by the Government of India in the matter of
 providing funds to Kolkata Port Trust for Capital Dredging. The Committee is surprised to note that on one side, the
 Government of India has, in principle, decided to fully reimburse the cost on items directly related to dredging and
 maintenance of River Hooghly as well as cost incurred on items directly related to maintenance dredging of Haldia
 Shipping Channel, where as, on other hand, the allocation for capital dredging has been reduced in a arbitrary manner.
 The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that there should be no constraint of funds for the Kolkata Port so far
 as dredging is concerned. Silting at Kolkata Port is problem of recurring nature therefore the actual requirement of fund
 for dredging and maintenance of River Hooghly and Haldia Shipping Channel be identified and provision be made at
 Budget Estimate stage itself.
 
ACTION TAKEN/PROPOSED TO BE TAKEN
 
22.       Since the Budget Estimates for 2002-03 had already been finalized, the matter for full reimbursement of the
 expenditure  incurred by the Port Trust based on audit certificates will be taken up with the Ministry of Finance during
 Revised Estimates stage.  However, the matter will be pursued with the Ministry of Finance for allocation of the entire
 requirement based on audit certificates, at Budget Estimates stage itself during 2003-04 and onwards.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
23.       The Committee was further informed by the Ministry of Shipping vide O.M. No.PD-11013/5/2002-US(I) dated
 4.12.2002 that Capital Dredging Project under the scheme “River Regulatory Measures” for improvement of the
 draught in the Hooghly estuary of Kolkata Port Trust was sanctioned by the Government of India in November, 2001. 
 The project envisages cutting a channel of approximately 10 kms. of length for a width of 200 mtrs. (at bottom) upto a
 depth of 4.5 mtrs.  below chart Datum by Capital Dredging through Jiggerkhali Flat along an alignment favourable to
 the flow of the river in this region.
 
24.       Tender for the major component of the work (capital dredging) was issued on five occasions but could not be
 finalized because of unwillingness of intending bidders to accept maintenance dredging for one year in the newly
 dredge cut channel, apprehension of bidders that they would not be able to guarantee the required depth within the
 estimated limit of quantity of dredging as well as possibility of failure to dredge and sustain the channel within the
 proposed alignment etc.  Due to its inability in freezing the techno-commercial deviations put forward by the bidders,
 Kolkata Port Trust has engaged National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai as consultant to review/refine
 the project in the light of present hydro-dynamic conditions of Hooghly estuary as well as to revise the technical part of
 the tender document after finalizing the recommendations.  NIOT have already started the work of reviewing the
 scheme and their report is expected by the end of December 2002.
 
25.       The Committee was further informed that Ministry of Shipping had a budgetary allocation of Rs.175 crores this
 year.  Unfortunately, on account of technical snag, Rs.175 crores has been surrendered at the R.E. stage.  The next
 meeting on Revised Estimate and Budget Estimate will take place after seven days.  The Ministry of Shipping have
 given proposal for about Rs.200 crores for raising the capital next year.  If the NIOT report comes, hopefully, by the
 end of December on schedule an entire technical tendering process would be facilitated.  Then there will be about 2-3
 months time when the operation can start.  Now, if the operations take about three months to start, then, probably the
 next financial year will come and, by that time, hopefully, the funds will not be problem. 
 
26.       The Committee is constrained to note that the Ministry of Shipping was unable to spend Rs.105 crores during
 this financial year and surrendered the said amount at Revised Estimate stage.  The Committee is of the opinion that
 capital dredging at Kolkata Port is a very important matter and needs time bound action plan.  Earlier, there was
 scarcity of the amount for the capital dredging at port, but now the Ministry is unable to spend the amount allocated for
 capital dredging, inspite of budgetary support from the Government of India.  The Committee, therefore, further
 recommends that the Ministry of Shipping should spend the allocated budgetary fund in a time bound manner and get
 prepared the action plan for capital dredging.

RECOMMENDATION (Para 48)
 
37.       The Committee observes that despite of alternative proposals suggested by the Cochin Port Trust, the Kochi
 Refineries Ltd. is adamant to go ahead with its plan for construction of Single Buoy Mooring (SBM) without giving a
 positive thought to the proposals. The Committee is of the opinion that both Public Sector undertakings are under
 administrative control of the Government of India and in absence of agreement, any loss incurred to the Cochin Port
 Trust will be the loss to the Nation. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its earlier recommendation made in its 52
nd
 report on Demands for Grants (2001-02) of the Ministry of Shipping and recommends that Ministries of Shipping and
 Petroleum and Natural Gas should evolve an amicable solution to the problem. Kochi Refinery Ltd. should consider, in
 the national interest, the alternative proposals suggested by the Cochin Port Trust before taking up the construction of
 the Single Buoy Mooring.

 constituted to interact with the officials of Kochi Refineries Limited to study and work out a feasible alternative
 logistics solution.  In response, Kochi Refineries Limited has also constituted a high level Committee to interact with
 the port officials.  Based on the deliberations so far, Cochin Port Trust has expressed the hope that they would be able
 to arrive at a mutually acceptable solution.

CENTRAL INLAND WATER TRANSPORT CORPORATION LTD. (CIWTC)
 
RAJABAGAN DOCKYAR (RBD)
 
RECOMMENDATION (Para 64)
 
52.       The Committee appreciates the steps and efforts taken by the Ministry of Shipping for revival of the Central
 Inland Water transport Corporation Ltd.  The Committee is of the view that expertise and facilities of ship repair and
 dry dock facilities at Rajabagan Dockyard should not go waste. The Committee, therefore, recommends that while
 taking steps for revival of Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd., the facilities of ship repair and Dry Dock
 available in Rajabagan Dockyard should be exploited fully so that assets and manpower engaged in those activities are
 utilised optimally. The Committee also expect that the present ambiguity with regard to future manpower in the
 Rajabagan Dockyard should be removed and the manpower requirement in Central Inland Water Transport Corporation
 Ltd. for the next five-years be firmed up and informed to all concerned including the Committee. 
 
ACTION TAKEN/PROPOSED TO BE TAKEN
 
53.       In the light of the Cabinet decision in June 2001, steps have been initiated for disposal of assets of Rajabagan
 Dockyard along with its land, buildings, plant, machineries and offering the advantage of its manpower resources.  The
 decision to close Rajabagan Dockyard of CIWTC was taken after considering various aspects and recommendations,
 including the report submitted by the consultant.  The idea is to ensure that the Corporation concentrates on its core
 activity of cargo movement.  The Government is fully aware that the productive assets of the Corporation have to be
 utilized to the optimum level.  Action has been initiated for disposal of land which is not directly relevant for the core
 activity of the Corporation.  With a view to rationalizing the manpower, a voluntary retirement scheme has been
 introduced in the Corporation and it is expected that 241 employees during 2001-02 and 2002-03 each and 168
 employees during 2003-04 will opt for VRS.  Even if Rajabagan Dockyard is sold, the manpower is likely to be utilized
 by the new owner.  A large number of employees of CIWTC including Rajabagan Dockyard have opted for the
 voluntary retirement scheme.  A rational assessment of the manpower requirement of the Corporation has been made
 and the VRS is expected to take care of the surplus manpower.

INTERNAL RATE OF RETURN (IRR)
 
RECOMMENDATION (Para 67)
 
55.       The Committee agrees to views of the Ministry of Shipping and is of the opinion that at present Inland Water
 Transport System in the country is at the initial stage of its development. The allocation of amount for any proposed
 scheme/project in the field of Inland water Transport Sector is for its infrastructure development. Therefore, there is
 very low scope for any Internal Rate of Return (IRR) from this Sector. The Committee therefore, recommends that the
 Government of India should review its approach for Inland water Transport Sector and should not insist for 12% IRR of
 any scheme/project in this field. The concept of Internal Rate of Return may ever be dispensed with as the benefits
 from such projects are passed on to the trade and economy.     
 
ACTION TAKEN/PROPOSED TO BE TAKEN
 
56.       Acting on this recommendation of the Committee all concerned agencies like Planning Commission and
 Ministry of Finance will be informed about the recommendation while seeking approval to the schemes/projects of the
 IWT sector.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
57.       The Committee notes the reply of the Government.
 
MARITIME TRAINING IN INDIA
 
RECOMMENDATION (Para 72)
 
58.       The Committee appreciates the proposal for establishment of an Indian Institute of Maritime Studies under
 Societies Registration Act, 1960 and placing the Government run Maritime Institutions within the domain of this
 Society. The move will certainly give a qualitative boost to the maritime training in the country. The Committee,
 however, recommends that the Government of India may consider to give the status to Indian Institute of Maritime
 Studies similar to that of IITs’ and introduce a central legislation accordingly at the earliest. 
 
ACTION TAKEN/PROPOSED TO BE TAKEN
 
59.            Necessary action to register the Indian Institute of Maritime Studies (IIMS) Mumbai as a Society under the
 Societies Registration Act, 1860 has been taken by the Government and the Directorate General of Shipping, Mumbai,
 has filed necessary papers in the office of Registrar.
 
60.       IITs are conceived as Institutes of National importance with a special role assigned to the President of India,
 whereas the IIMS to begin with is being established as a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860
 and not under a separate Act of Parliament as in the case of IITs.  It is expected that once the Society starts functioning,
 it will soon be on its own and can gradually move towards a situation where conversion to a ‘deemed University’ or a
 ‘University’ or separate status under a special Act can be considered.  Thus, IIMS is seen as foreunner to its being
 converted to a higher status.
 
61.            However, many of the provisions of IIMS have similarities with the provisions of IITs.
 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
62.       The Committee notes the reply of the Government.

RECOMMENDATION (Para 78)
 
63.       The Committee is not satisfied with the attitude and approach of the Government of India is respect of Shipping
 Corporation of India Ltd. On one hand, the Government of India has taken decision to go for disinvestment in SCI,
 whereas on other side, Shipping Corporation of India Ltd. has expansion plan for acquisition of vessels during the year
 of 2002-03 involving an amount of Rs. 647.84 crores for investment.  The Committee fails to understand as to why the
 decision for disinvestment of Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) has taken place when SCI is able to manage its
 activities through its own resources.
 
ACTION TAKEN/PROPOSED TO BE TAKEN
 
64.            Disinvestment of Shipping Corporation of India Ltd. (SCI) is in accordance with the Government’s overall
 policy to disinvest its stake in non-strategic Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs).  Regular business plans, including
 acquisition of assets, are normally not put on hold pending disinvestment.  It is part of the SCI’s corporate plan, which
 has been approved by the Planning Commission as well.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
65.       The Committee notes the reply of the Government.
 
RECOMMENDATION (Para 79 and 80)
 
66.       On enquiry from the Ministry regarding revaluation of assets of SCI, the Committee was informed that no
 revaluation has taken place, so far, since process of disinvestment started.
 
67.       The Committee fails to understand why the SCI has not revalued its assets as the matter of disinvestment of SCI
 has been under consideration for the last 3-4 years. Owner should be aware of its assets value when a major part of it is
 being disposed of.
 
ACTION TAKEN/PROPOSED TO BE TAKEN
 
68.       As per the prevailing practice, the assets of a going concern like SCI, are not required to be revalued
 periodically.  Such revaluation is generally undertaken at the time of merger/acquisitions involving change of
 ownership or change in management control.  In the case of SCI, no such revaluation has been done so far.  In the
 context of the proposed disinvestment however, a detailed asset valuation exercise is being carried out, which will be
 kept in view while fixing the reserve price for strategic sale of SCI.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
69.       The Ministry in its further reply vide O.M. No.SD-11018/4/2002-MD dated 5.12.2002 informed the Committee
 that presently, Government equity in SCI is 80.12%.  Government has now decided to disinvest 51% of the equity share
 capital of SCI to a strategic partner along with Management control.  Action is in progress by the Ministry of

70.       The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Government.  The Committee is surprised to note that on
 one side Government of India are prepared to sell Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), where as, on other side SCI
 does not know about the value of its assets.  The Committee is unable to understand the reasons for not doing the

 recommendation that Shipping Corporation of India should make revaluation of its assets.
 
COASTAL SHIPPING IN INDIA
 
RECOMMENDATION (Para 84)
 
71.       The Committee is unhappy to note that during 9
th Five year plan no special attention was given on coastal
 shipping which is one of the most energy efficient, eco-friendly and cheap modes of transport for movement of bulk
 commodities over long distances. Considering the vast coastline and congestion on land routes, the costal shipping
 offers an effective alternative means of Transport. Despite this, no adequate policy measures have been taken by the
 Ministry. There are 184 minor/intermediate ports in the country along the 5560 kms coastline of India.
 Minor/intermediate ports can play important role in the coastal Shipping. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
 Ministry of Shipping should frame a comprehensive policy and prepare plans to promote the coastal shipping in the
 country. 
 
ACTION TAKEN/PROPOSED TO BE TAKEN
 
72.       The Government has taken various measures to develop coastal shipping in the country.  As a measure to
 encourage its development, coastal ships and sailing vessels have been exempted from payment of lightdues. 
 Instructions have been issued to all Major Ports (except Calcutta Port Trust who has provided a separate birth for
 coastal ships) to grant priority berthing to coastal ships without priority berthing charges.  The Central Board of
 Exercise and Customs have issued instructions permitting sanction of drawback as the port of loading after shipment of
 goods.  The Coastal fleet in the country has increased.  It stood at 329 ships with GRT of 7,31,367 as on 31.12.2001.  A
 proposal to declare coastal shipping as an infrastructure industry was also taken up with the Ministry of Finance, but the
 same was not agreed to.
 
73.       It has since been decided by the Government to conduct a combined study on development of coastal shipping
 and minor ports.  The proposed study will identify cargo that can be diverted to coastal shipping from other modes of
 transport, evaluate future traffic potential for coastal movement in the next 10 years and explore the possibility of
 developing new routes to meet the existing and potential demands.  The study will identify minor ports for use by
 coastal shipping, keeping in view the rail/road connectivity and recommend the infrastructure needed at such ports.  It
 will also examine the possibility of establishing an integrated transport system between coastal ships and Inland Water
 Transport.  It will prepare a plan of action and give broad coast estimates thereof.  The proposal for award of the study
 is under process.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
74.
              While noting the reply of the Government, the Committee takes serious view over refusal by the Ministry of
 Finance to declare coastal shipping as an infrastructure industry.  The Committee is of the view that the
 coastal shipping is, at present, in the initial stage and requires comprehensive policy.  To declare, coastal
 shipping as an infrastructure industry is a first step towards its promotion.  The Committee, therefore,
 further recommends that the coastal shipping should be declared as an infrastructure industry.   The
 Committee further recommends that proposal for award of combined study on development of coastal
 shipping and minor ports be processed, expeditiously.

R E P O R T
 
            The Hotel Corporation of India Limited (HCI), a public limited company wholly owned by Air India Limited
 and was incorporated on July 8, 1971, under the Companies Act, 1956.  It was established when Air India decided to
 enter the hotel industry in keeping with the then prevalent trend among world airlines.  Its main objective was to offer
 to the passengers a better product, both at the international airports and at other places of tourist interest, thereby also
 increasing tourism in India.  Air India also aimed to cater to the requirement of in-flight catering as well as to provide
 quality hotel accommodation to the passengers and crew.  Since then Hotel Corporation of India was operating four
 hotels, in Mumbai (two), Delhi (one) and Srinagar (one), one Hotel at Rajgir and two flight catering units in Mumbai
 and Delhi.
           
2.         The Annual Report 2001-2002 of Ministry of Civil Aviation contains a chapter on Hotel Corporation of India. 
 While highlighting the main functions/achievements of HCI, the chapter gives the following details with regard to the
 Centaur Hotel Mumbai Airport, Mumbai :-
 
            “The first hotel of the Company, namely the Centaur Hotel Bombay Airport was commissioned in
 May 1975.  The Hotel at Mumbai Airport has 288 rooms including 4 Deluxe Suites, a 24 hour Coffee
 Shop, 2 Speciality Restaurants, Bar, Shopping Arcade, Health Club, Swimming Pool, Beauty Parlour,
 Banquet and Conference facilities for the transit passengers etc.  The hotel right from its inception, was
 well received by the airlines, travel agents and business travellers and has had a high occupancy, the
 hotel is extremely popular and has a reputation for excellent food.  60 Guest Rooms alongwith its
 connected Shafts and corridors were renovated in December, 2000.
 
Additional 60 guest rooms alongwith its connected shafts and corridors are now under renovation
 and expected to be completed by the end of February, 2002.”
           
3.         During October 2002, there were reports in the electronic/print media that Centaur Hotel Mumbai Airport
 (CHMA), sold by the Government to Batra Hospitalities for Rs.83 crores had been later resold by the latter to the
 Sahara Group for Rs.115 crores.  Almost all national dailies and magazines covered articles in this regard.  The issue
 was also raised in the Parliament and a marathon debate on the subject was held in the Parliament during its Winter
 Session in the year 2002 wherein replying to a query on the subject, the Minister of Disinvestment, Shri Arun Shourie,

 Airports Authority of India.  The Committee brought to the notice of Ministry of Civil Aviation that turnover levy
 payable to Airports Authority of India was reduced from 6 per cent to 2 per cent on the direction of the Ministry of
 Disinvestment with a plea that such remission will fetch attractive price of the property even when Ministry of Civil
 Aviation was not in favour of such decision.  The Committee enquired from the Ministry of Civil Aviation as to what
 was the impact of such reduction to the revenue of Airports Authority of India and how the loss of such revenue of

 first round not many bidders submitted their financial bids.  There will be reduction in revenue to Airports Authority of

20.       As regards refixing of the reserve price, the Committee was informed that J.P. Morgan (India) Private Limited
 (formerly Jardine Fleming India Securities Limited) had submitted separate valuation reports before and after reduction
 of the levy.  The valuation reports for CHMA were submitted to Ministry of Disinvestment on November 5, 2001 and
 January 18, 2002 before the submission of first and second round of financial bids for CHMA.  The lease rentals were
 reduced from 6 per cent to 2 per cent of the turnover prior to the invitation of the second round of financial bids.  This
 was the only parameter that was altered between the first and second valuation reports and the valuations were modified
 accordingly.  These reports are available with the Ministry of Disinvestment.  On both occasions, the reserve price was
 determined by the Valuation Committee constituted by Government of India and the valuation reports formed a part of
 consideration for determination of the reserve price.  Reserve price with 6 per cent turnover levy was Rs.76.2 crores
 and with 2 per cent, turnover levy Rs.78.3 crores. 
 
21.       The Committee observes that the reduction of turnover levy from 6 per cent to 2 per cent which entails the
 reduction of revenue of Airports Authority of India, has been aimed to ensure better price of CHMA.  To get a better
 price for the benefit of AI, the Government has taken a route which leads to a loss of revenue to another Government
 company.  The loss to AAI for this reduction of rate of turnover levy from 6 per cent to 2 per cent has been reported to
 be approximately Rs.17 crores.  Applying the Net Present Value method (with IRR factor 7 per cent which was higher
 than the bank rate), the loss comes to Rs.5.58 crores.   To compensate such a loss the reserve price has been increased
 by Rs.2.1 crores only from Rs.76.2 crores to Rs.78.3 crores.  The Committee is of the view that the issue required
 further clarification and investigation.

TRANSFER OF THE PETROL PUMP
 
30.       The Committee also took note of a controversy that arose over the actual ownership of a petrol pump, which was
 located in the premises of Centaur Hotel Mumbai Airport.  The Committee enquired from the Ministry of Civil
 Aviation regarding the details of the assets considered for physical valuation and whether the petrol pump was also
 included in the valuation.
 
31.       The Ministry of Civil Aviation replied that all the assets of HCI were valued by the Asset Valuer.  The petrol
 pump and its equipments did not belong to HCI which only had dealership of the petrol pump. Therefore, the Asset
 Valuer did not value the petrol pump.  The revenue from the petrol pump dealership was taken into account by the
 Advisors for determining the value of CHMA under different methods.
 
32.       However, the Committee noted that in the status note furnished vide  their O.M. No.13/2/2002-F.I dated the 18
th
 December, the Ministry of Civil Aviation stated that at the time of transfer of business of Centaur Hotel Mumbai
 Airport on 5.6.2002, the petrol pump, which was also a part of the transaction, was transferred to M/s Batra Hospitality
 Pvt. Ltd. (BHPL) on ‘as is where is’ basis.  The Joint Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation  (Shri Sanat Kaul) requested
 the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas for transferring of the dealership of I.O.C. for the said petrol pump to M/s.
 Batra Hospitality Pvt. Ltd.  The petrol pump was operated by M/s BHPL till 4.10.2002 when IOC informed HCI vide
 letter No.MSO/R/4340 dated 27.9.2002 that the dealership agreement dated 16.3.1975 executed between HCI and IOC
 stands terminated with immediate effect.  Since HCI had already effected the physical transfer of the petrol pump
 alongwith the hotel w.e.f. 5.6.2002, BHPL were requested to take up the matter with India Oil Corporation. 
 
33.       From the position furnished by the Ministry of Civil Aviation, it is quite clear that the petrol pump was owned
 by the IOC, another PSU under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.  The Committee is unable to understand as
 to how the Ministry of Civil Aviation could get the valuation done and also proceed to transfer the ownership of the
 petrol pump without the consent of the concerned PSU and the Ministry.  The Committee is of the view that neither the
 Ministry of Disinvestment nor the Hotel Corporation of India had the right to transfer the petrol pump to M/s. Batra
 Hospitalities Pvt. Ltd. since neither of them were the owners of the petrol pump.  This clearly reflects that no proper
 thought was given to the selling process by the Government before inviting the Expression of Interest for the properties
 of HCI.

 dated the 18
th December 2002 informed the Committee that in response to a query of Ministry of Disinvestment, Shri
 A.L. Batra informed on 18 th October 2002 that 100 per cent shares of CHMA had been transferred to Sahara Group.

 Agreement nor any benefits or burdens under this Agreement shall be assigned by either Party without the prior written
 consent of the other Party”.  The Committee, therefore, enquired from the Ministry whether the transfer of 100 per cent
 shareholding of BHPL to Sahara Group was an assignment in disguise, the legality of the transfer of shareholding to the

 the Attorney General of India (copy at Annexure-6) on the matter which inter-alia brings out that there was no
 obligation on BHPL to obtain any prior consent as contemplated by Article 13.4 of the Agreement to Sell and hence,
 there has been no breach of the Lease Agreement.

 Lease Agreement with regard to the re-sale of CHMA.  However, keeping in view the experience and to stop such
 quick change of hands at a premium, necessary provisions may be incorporated in the Agreement to Sell in respect of

 brought out with regard to the selection criteria, reduction of turnover levy, rebidding process and the transfer of petrol

REDUCTION OF TURNOVER LEVY
The Committee observes that the reduction of turnover levy from 6 per cent to 2 per cent which entails the reduction of
 revenue of Airports Authority of India, has been aimed to ensure better price of CHMA.  To get a better price for the
 benefit of AI, the Government has taken a route which leads to a loss of revenue to another Government company.  The
 loss to AAI for this reduction of rate of turnover levy from 6 per cent to 2 per cent has been reported to be

REBIDDING PROCESS
 
The Committee is not convinced with the reply furnished by the Ministry of Civil Aviation that “Unless the shortlisting
 criteria were changed, it was unlikely that any new bidder would have shown interest”.  It may be pointed out that
 initially there were 17 parties who were short listed out of 19 parties who submitted EOI and subsequently 4 parties
 have participated in due diligence.  Hence, there was a qualitative change in the offer by reducing the turnover levy
 from 6 per cent to 2 per cent.  The contention of the Ministry of Civil Aviation that it was unlikely that any new bidder
 would have shown interest is, therefore, not tenable.
(Para 27)
 
The Committee is of the view that the idea of reduction in turnover levy was to go for re-bidding by exploring ways and
 means to secure better response for re-invited bid.  But, by restricting the invitation of the 2
nd round bid among the four
 parties only, the very purpose of reduction in turnover levy was defeated as only one bidder, that too the same for the
 earlier bid, remained in picture. Also, no thought was given to the views expressed by Shri R. C. Aggarwal.  The
 second round of bidding was, therefore, clearly a case of considering a ‘single bid’.
(Para 28)
 
The Committee feels that the ground rules for participating in the bidding process, as prescribed in the original
 advertisement inviting EOI for the properties of HCI, were framed in such a restrictive manner that it allowed hoteliers
 only in the bidding process.  As a result, the market for the properties of HCI could not be fully explored and several
 other interested parties, who were interested in offering better prices for the properties of HCI, could not enter the
 bidding process.  The Committee also feels that the 100 per cent shareholding of BHPL, which took over CHMA has
 been acquired by Sahara Group with the sole intention of taking over the business of CHMA within a short span of just
 6 months of taking over of CHMA by Shri A. L. Batra.  This clearly shows that there were interested parties for CHMA
 which were not properly explored, disproving the contention of the Ministry of Civil Aviation that it was unlikely that a
 new bidder would have shown interest.  The Committee feels that the reason why only a single bid was considered even
 after reducing the turnover levy, needs to be investigated.

TRANSFER OF THE PETROL PUMP
 
33.       From the position furnished by the Ministry of Civil Aviation, it is quite clear that the petrol pump was owned
 by the IOC, another PSU under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.  The Committee is unable to understand as
 to how the Ministry of Civil Aviation could get the valuation done and also proceed to transfer the ownership of the
 petrol pump without the consent of the concerned PSU and the Ministry.  The Committee is of the view that neither the
 Ministry of Disinvestment nor the Hotel Corporation of India had the right to transfer the petrol pump to M/s. Batra
 Hospitalities Pvt. Ltd. since neither of them were the owners of the petrol pump.  This clearly reflects that no proper
 thought was given to the selling process by the Government before inviting the Expression of Interest for the properties

1                    INTRODUCTION
 
1.1      Hotel Corporation of India Limited ("HCI") is a wholly owned subsidiary of Air India. Air India entered the hotel
 business in order to promote tourism in the country and to cater to the requirement of in-flight catering as well as to
 provide quality hotel accommodation to the passengers and crew. HCI was incorporated on July 8, 1971 with the
 objective of carrying on business of operating hotels and flight kitchens. HCI was operating four hotels, in Mumbai
 (two), Delhi (one) and Sringar (one), one hotel at Rajgir and two flight-catering units in Mumbai and Delhi.
2          RECOMMENDATION OF DISINVESTMENT COMMISSION
2.1      The Disinvestment Commission, in its 6
th Report published in December 1997, presented its recommendations in
 respect of disinvestment of Hotel Corporation of India (HCI).  It recommended that hotels at Mumbai and Delhi be sold
 as separate units through a transparent and competitive bidding process after undertaking a proper valuation through a
 Financial Adviser.
2.2      For hotel at Srinagar, the management of Air India may initiate dialogue with J&K Government in order to exit
 from its ownership. It was suggested that since lands on which the two airport hotels at Mumbai and Delhi are located
 belong to the AAI, Air India would need to negotiate and settle the terms of transfer with AAI prior to the sale.
2.3      It further suggested that Air India may decide whether the flight catering services should continue to be provided
 by HCI or whether it should be sold as independent units through a transparent competitive bidding process like the
 process of sale of Hotels.
2.4      The Commission in its 5
th Report had clarified that disinvestment in a subsidiary company of a PSU should be
 decided by the Board of Management of the concerned PSU.
 
3.         Follow-up Action on the Recommendations of Disinvestment Commission:
3.1      Air-India in its Board Meeting held in July 1998 considered the recommendation of the Disinvestment
 Commission and decided to accept in principle the dis-investment in HCI. However, the actual modalities of
 disinvestment were to be decided on the receipt of the report of a Consultant which was to be appointed by the Air
 India Board. The Department of Disinvestment, in its note dated 12.2.2000 regarding disinvestment of Government
 equity in Air India inter-alia, sought the approval of the Cabinet Committee on Disinvestment (CCD) so that the
 revenue realized accrues to Air India. The CCD, in its meeting held on 26.5.2000 took note of the proposal.
3.2      It was also decided to sort out the long pending issues of settlement of lease terms for the lease of AAI land at
 Mumbai and Delhi Airports for which there were no formal agreements. Shri Sanat Kaul, Joint Secretary, Ministry of
 Civil Aviation was appointed as sole Arbitrator in September, 1999 and after going through the records and hearing
 both AAI and AI/HCI gave his award in end November 1999 and suggested for execution of fresh lease deeds for a
 period of about 30 years. In the said award, he suggested that HCI should settle the dues with AAI and also pay the
 turnover levy of 2% for the years HCI made profits (for the past) and AAI should also agree for sub-letting in view of
 the disinvestment of these properties to the prospective buyers or entering into fresh lease on the terms like the case of
 Radisson in Delhi and Leela hotels in Mumbai on market terms.

REPORT
 
The Department of Tourism is the nodal agency for the formulation of national policies and programmes on
 Tourism and for the coordination of activities of various Central Government agencies, State Governments/UTs and the
 Private Sector for the development and promotion of tourism in the country.  The Department of Tourism plays a
 crucial role in coordinating and supplementing the efforts of the State/Union Territory Governments catalyzing
 investment, strengthening promotional and marketing efforts and private in providing training manpower resources.
 The main activities of the Department are: -
 
i)
                  Policy formulation and planning
ii)                Co-ordination
iii)               Regulation
iv)              Infrastructure and Product development
v)                Human Resource Development
vi)              Publicity, Marketing and Facilitation
vii)             Research, Analysis, Monitoring and Evaluation
viii)           International Co-operation and External Assistance
ix)              Parliament work
x)                Management of Public Sector Undertakings and Autonomous bodies
 
2.         The Department of Tourism is headed by a Secretary.  The post of Director General (Tourism) has been merged
 with the post of Secretary (T) who is assisted by the Joint Secretary and the Additional Director General. In addition to
 the Headquarters Organisation at New Delhi, the Directorate General of Tourism has 21 India tourism Offices in India
 (including 5 Regional Offices), situated at Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Agra, Bhubaneshwar, Aurangabad,
 Bangalore, Cochin, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Imphal, Jaipur, Khajuraho, Naharlagun, Panaji (Goa), Patna, Port Blair,
 Shillong, Varanasi and Thiruvananthapuram.  There are 13 India tourism Offices Overseas, which include 5 Regional
 offices at Sydney, New York, Tokyo, Frankfurt and Dubai.  The other India tourism Offices are located at Los Angeles,
 London, Toronto, Paris, Amsterdam, Milan, Singapore and Johannesburg.

13.       A tourist circuit is defined as a route on which at least three major tourists destinations are located in such a
 manner that none of these are in the same town, village or city.  At the same time they are not ­­­­separated by a large
 distance  so that a tourist would not like to cover them in a sequence.  The scheme is basically a merger of all the

 employment. India’s share of global domestic tourism is much higher (around 4.6% of estimated global domestic

th Five Year Plan, the Department of Tourism sanctioned

 put forth by the Department of Tourism for delay i.e. lack of coordination between the State Government and different
 other Ministries in the implementation of projects, besides low level of monitoring and review of progress.  The
 Committee is of the opinion that involvement of Members of Parliament in identification, development and monitoring
 of tourist destinations in their respective state, can avoid delay and cost overrun in execution of tourism projects. In this
 connection, the committee reiterates its earlier recommendation made in 55
th Report, which is reproduced below;
 
“The Committee recommends that the Department of Tourism should involve the Members of Parliament in
 the identification and development of places of tourist interest in their respective states.  The Committee is of
 the view that, as elected representatives of the people, Members of Parliament can also help the Department in
 identifying tourism sports in their states and inform the Department of Tourism which can take steps to
 develop such tourism areas.  The Committee also recommends that the Department of Tourism should, by
 way of taking the initiative, request the Members of Parliament to identify places, which can be developed as
 tourist spots.  The Members of Parliament should also be kept informed of the status of the tourism projects in
 their respective states.”

 Parliament in identification, development and monitoring process of tourists destinations/circuits in their respective
 states and have a task force which will coordinate between different Ministries as well as State Governments and
 respective Members of Parliament in that state for monitoring the progress of physical targets every quarter or so.

57.       The eight States of North East and Sikkim are endowed with diverse tourist attractions.  The rich natural beauty,
 serenity and exotic flora of the area are invaluable resources for development of eco-tourism in the region.  The
 Department of Tourism attaches great importance to the development of tourism infrastructure in the North East region
 in view of immense tourist potential of the region and announced host of incentives/concessions for development of
 tourism in the region.  The Department of Tourism has launched a nationwide campaign to promote the domestic
 tourist to visit the North East State.  Direct flights have also been inducted between Guwahati and Bangkok and also
 excellent connections from Kolkata to South East Asian region has also been opened.
 
58.       The attention of the Department of Tourism was invited to the declared policy of the Government to earmark
 10% of the budgetary allocation to the developmental projects in the North East Region including Sikkim.  During

 Annual Plan Rs.32.5 crores has been allocated for the region.  However, the Department of Tourism did not indicate
 anything about the amount spent on the developmental activities undertaken in the North East Region. It was submitted
 to the Committee that the Government attaches great importance to the development of tourist infrastructure in the
 North East region in view of immense tourist potential of the region.  Accordingly, Department of Tourism has focused
 on utilization of budget allocation of Rs.22.50 crores to complete the ongoing projects and upgradation of various
 tourist facilities.  In order to develop and promote tourism in the region, the Department of Tourism has taken
 following steps for the year    2003-04: -

 and promotion of tourism in all the States in the country including North Eastern Region.

 tourism potential of this region. Therefore, the Committee recommends that the tourism related developmental work
 undertaken in the North East region should be given the highest priority and recommends that the funds allocated for
 the North East region should be optimally utilised in that region only.

THE APPROACH IN THE 10
TH PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 2003-04
 
The Committee is happy to note that the plan allocation of Rs.225.00 crores of the Department of Tourism was not
 subjected to any reduction at R.E. stage during 2002-2003 and the outlay for the year 2003-2004 has also been hiked
 substantially from Rs.225.00 crores to Rs.325.00 crores.  The Committee hopes that the maximum amount of plan
 outlay would be utilised properly and substantially during the first five months of the current financial year so that the
 Department will be in a position to make demand for more allocation of funds at R.E. stage   for development of
 tourism infrastructure and promotion of tourism in the country.
 
The Committee notes that for the financial year 2002-03, the expenditure upto January 2003 has been only 55% i.e.
 Rs.124.876 crores out of the total plan allocation of Rs.225 crores.  Though, the Department of Tourism have assured
 that the total allocation would be spent by the end of the financial year i.e. 31st March 2003 the Committee however, is
 unable to understand as to how the Department would be able to spend the remaining 45% of the plan allocation within
 a short span of just 2 months of the financial year.  The Committee therefore, disapproves the tendency of spending
 funds desperately towards the end of the financial year. The Committee recommends that the Department should evolve
 some mechanism of uniform utilization pattern through out the year so as to avoid incurring expenditure at the fag end
 of the financial year.
(Paras 7 and 9)

The Committee is happy to note that Department of Tourism is taking a holistic approach for development of these six
 tourist circuits in the country on each year and providing necessary infrastructural facilities within these circuits and
 convergence of resources in coordination with States/Private sector.  The Committee also notes that Department of

 importance for the development of tourism in the country and concentrate on the development of important travel
 circuits alone.  The Committee recommends that more tourist circuits region wise covering more than a State/UT may
 be selected and developed on the basis of the tourism potential of the places according to international standards and
 aggressive marketing efforts may be taken up in order to attract more and more tourists to these places. 
(Para 15)

The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Department of Tourism for improving existing products and developing
 new tourism products to world-class standards by providing assistance to State Governments/UTs.  The Committee
 feels that this sector in the past was given low priority by the Government as a result of which it was loosing
 competitive edge.  The committee hopes that the work at six selected destinations will be completed with in a stipulated

 Department of Tourism should prioritise the projects, which would help in strengthening of infrastructure and product
 development in the country besides harnessing the national development priorities.

The Rural Tourism is a new market concept to tap tourist traffic as it can form the perfect vehicle for achievement of the
 national objective of achieving partnerships between local communities, government and industry.  Besides, it would
 help generate employment at local level, dispensing with the need of migrations to distant places for earning livelihood
 thereby leading to economic betterment. The Rural Tourism can also provide a solution to the increasing trends of
 industrialization and help in countering the stress of urban life styles and other urbanization syndromes. The Committee
 feels that global tourism growth potential can be harnessed as a strategy for Rural Development and therefore,
 recommends that the Department of Tourism should develop a strong platform around the concept of Rural Tourism for
 achieving the national objectives in better perspective.
(Para 24)

The Committee notes that sufficient funds have been earmarked and support in the form of grants to act as a catalyst has
 also been provided to large revenue generating projects like convention centers, luxury trains, cruise terminals,
 ropeways, cruise vessels. The Committee however, couldn’t understand as to how the scheme has been finalized when
 the proposals under the scheme are yet to be received by the department of tourism. It shows that the Department is
 lacking pro-active  approach in the matter, which could result in non-utilisation of plan outlay earmarked for the
 scheme. The Committee therefore recommends that the Department of Tourism should take expeditious steps to
 activate the State Governments so that the States send their proposals under the scheme quickly to ensure that plan
 outlay allocated be utilized by the State Tourism Development Corporation or any such public body or institution as
 equity to projects to be promoted by them or in private sector projects.

The Committee appreciates the scheme launched by the Department of Tourism for training the persons in an
 unorganized sector consisting of small hotel, dhabas and restaurant and other eatable joints spread all over the country
 including tourists guides. The Committee is of the opinion since tourism industry plays a nodal role in displaying the
 rich cultural heritage to the world at large, and possesses high employment potential, personnel engaged in this sector
 are different from those required by personnel engaged in other sectors.  The Committee hopes that this would
 adequately cater to the training needs of the persons engaged in the unorganized sector and helps them is upgrading
 their quality.  The Committee desires that sufficient funds should be allocated under this head and efforts should be
 made to make the scheme more effective by expanding its coverage to the important tourist circuits/tourist destinations.
(Para 29)

INTRODUCTION
 
            The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is responsible for development, formulation and implementation
 of policies relating to Road Transport and National Highways.  Its main function relate to road development and
 maintenance including Border Roads, Planning and co-ordination and Road Transport.
 
2.         The Ministry is administratively divided into two wings namely Transport Wing and Roads Wing.
 
3.         Transport Wing is concerned with the formulation of broad policies relating to Road Transport, Motor Vehicles
 Act, legislation relating to Road Transport Corporations, besides making arrangements for movement of motor
 vehicular traffic with the neighbouring countries.
 
4.         Roads Wing is mainly concerned with the matters relating to:-
 
Advising Government on all general policy matters relating to Highways;
 
Development & Maintenance of roads declared as National Highways;
 
Roads other than National Highways in Union Territories;
 
Administration of Central Road Fund (CRF) pertaining to State Roads other than rural roads;
 
Evaluation of standards for roads and bridges and formulation of specifications;
 
Performance of road research;
 
National Highways Authority of India and National Institute for Training of Highway Engineers.
 
5.         The following autonomous bodies function under the administrative control of the Ministry of Road Transport &
 Highways :-
 
National Highways Authority of India (NHAI); and
National Institute of Training of Highway Engineers (NITHE).

 financial year 2003-04, was considered by the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport,

NATIONAL HIGHWAY DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (NHDP)
 
14.       Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has informed that the present emphasis of the Government is on
 improvement of Riding Quality of National Highways and for providing comforts to the road users.  Apart from
 National Highways Development Programme (NHDP), there is about 44,000 kms. of National Highways maintenance
 of which is being carried out from the funds available from Budget.  Since 1999, Riding Quality of about 29,000 kms.
 length have been improved by utilising funds allocated under both Plan and Non-Plan heads.  Riding Quality of the
 balance length is targeted to be completed within the next two years.
 
15.       The Government has embarked upon a massive National Highways Development Project (NHDP) in the
 country.  The NHDP is largest highways project ever undertaken in the country.  Under this project about 13,146 kms.
 of National Highways are proposed to be 4 to 6 laned at a total estimated cost of Rs.54,000 crores (at 1999 prices). 
 This is being implemented by NHAI.  The NHDP consists of following two components:-
 
Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) comprising of National Highways connecting four metro cities viz., Delhi, Mumbai,
 Chennai and Kolkata.  Total length of GQ is 5846 kms.  Four laning of 1159 kms. has already been completed and
 work is going on the remaining length except of 84 kms. of Allahabad bypass, which would also be awarded shortly.  
 The Golden Quadrilateral is targeted for substantial completion by December 2003.
 
North-South and East-West corridors comprising the National Highways connecting Srinagar to Kanyakumari including
 Kochi-Salem spur and Silchar to Porbandar.  The total length of the corridors is about 7300 kms.  Four/six laning of
 817 kms. has already been completed and work on 671 kms. is under implementation.  Work on 2500 kms. will start
 next year.  The target for the completion of the corridors is December 2007. 
 
16.       The Committee enquired from the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways regarding the physical achievements
 made in the Golden Quadrilateral Project so far and whether the Government expected the project to be completed
 within the targeted period.
 
17.       The Committee was informed by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways that the four-laning of the Golden
 Quadrilateral (GQ) component of the National Highway Development Project (NHDP) covers a total length of 5846
 kms. and was targeted for completion by December 2004.  It is expected that GQ will be completed within the targeted
 period, except for some contracts which may spill over to early part of 2005.  The projects which will spill over to 2005
 are mostly funded by World Bank.  The World Bank has its own procedures which had to be complied with and most
 of the contracts could be awarded only in March 2002 with a direction for completion of these contracts within a period
 of 36 months i.e. upto March 2005.  Contracts for 136 kms. are yet to be awarded.  Out of these, one package of 52
 kms. was held up due to a court case.  Of the total GQ length of 5846 kms., 1327 kms. have already been 4-laned and
 another 1320 kms. will be 4-laned by December, 2003 (i.e. a total length of 2647 kms.).

42.       The Committee is not convinced with the reasons advanced by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for
 collecting toll on roads and bridges in perpetuity.  The Committee feels that the Government is not justified in

 Committee had also commented upon this matter in its 43
rd Report on Demands for Grants 2000-2001 of the then
 Ministry of Surface Transport.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that once the cost of construction of a
 road/bridge plus interest is recovered, the collection of toll should be stopped.   The Committee also feels that there
 exists a need for the rationalisation of the toll tax being charged on the National Highways.  The Committee
 recommends that persons travelling on smaller stretches of the National Highways where toll is being collected should
 be charged a lower amount than the persons using the entire length of that National Highway.

PROBLEM OF OVERLOADING
 
59.       The share of Road Transport in Cargo Movement has gone up from only 12% in the year 1950-51 to now about
 65%.  The number of goods vehicles has gone up from 80,000 in the year 1950-51 to 26.8 lakhs by the year 2000 and is
 now estimated to be around 30 lakhs.
 
60.       The pavement design of road is based on the cumulative number of standard axle loads and therefore, higher
 axle load cause premature distress on the road pavements which in turn increases the maintenance cost of Indian roads. 
 An overloaded vehicle causes higher pollution besides inflicting high vehicle operating costs.  Moreover overloading is
 also a potential hazard not only to the driver of such vehicles but also to other road users.
 
61.       During the course of the evidence, the Committee drew the attention of the representatives of the Ministry of
 Road Transport & Highways to the ever-growing problem of overloading of vehicles, particularly trucks.  The
 Committee had also commented upon the matter in its 59
th Report on Demands for Grants 2002-03 of the Ministry of
 Road Transport & Highways.  The Committee also referred to the recommendations made in this context in its 59th
 Report and was of the view that the reply furnished by the Ministry had not been satisfactory.
 
62.       The Committee enquired from the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways as to whether the problem of
 overloading of vehicles was discussed during the meeting of Transport Development Council (TDC) and what remedial
 steps had been undertaken by the Ministry to tackle the problem of overloading of vehicles.  In their reply, the Ministry
 of Road Transport & Highways stated that the issue of overloading was discussed in the 30
th Meeting of Transport
 Development Council (TDC) held on 16.1.2003 and the following decisions were arrived at:
 
(a)        Strict enforcement of the provisions relating to overloading under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and Central
 Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989.
 
(b)        The State Governments are not to issue special cards/passes which legalise overloading.
 
(c)        The decision of the 28
th meeting of TDC held on 10.10.1998 for States to give a 25% tax rebate to popularise
 use of multi axle vehicles, which has been implemented so far by a few States like Karnataka, West Bengal,
 Meghalaya, Uttar Pradesh, Tripura and Gujarat may be carried out by other States also.

COMPUTERISATION OF ROAD TRANSPORT SECTOR
 
66.       During the course of the evidence the Committee enquired about the progress achieved with regard to the
 computerization of the road transport sector.  The Committee also drew the attention of the representatives of the
 Ministry of Road Transport & Highways towards the lack of uniformity in the issuance of driving licenses in the
 various parts of the country and enquired about the procedure for issue of driving licenses.
 
67.       In their reply the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways stated that standardized software for both front-end
 and back-end computerization of the RTO Offices in the country have been made available to all the States/UTs.  The
 back-end computerization envisages computerization of the existing records of Driving License (DL) and Registration
 Certificate (RC) of the motor vehicles.  The front-end computerization envisages issuance of Driving License and

 Registration Certificate on a Smart Card medium by the States/UTs.  The Ministry has been constantly urging the
 States and UTs to expeditiously undertake both front-end and back-end computerization. As per information available,
 back end computerization of more than 70 RTO offices has been completed or is nearing completion.
 
68.       As regards the procedure for issue of driving licenses, the Committee was informed that under the Motor
 Vehicles Act, 1988 the procedure is for grant of a learner’s license initially.  Thereafter, a normal driving license is
 issued.  These provisions are uniformly applicable throughout the country. The applicant is required to pass the
 prescribed test to the satisfaction of the Regional Transport Authority Officers (RTO) before such a license is issued. 
 The procedure and format of the license have been spelt out under Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
 
69.       The Licensing Authority has to satisfy itself about the competence of the person undertaking driving test to
 negotiate the various tests prescribed.  A driving license can be issued (i) on paper, (ii) on laminated plastic card or (iii)
 on a smart card.  On many occasions licenses are tampered with.  In some other cases persons have acquired more than
 one driving license.  In order to introduce a foolproof system for driving licenses standardized software specifications
 for the Smart Card have been prepared in consultation with NIC and made available free of cost to all the States.  Use
 of standardized software would ensure their readability and inter-operability throughout the country.  The Ministry has
 been requesting the State Governments to introduce Smart Card based documents at an early date and some States like
 Maharashtra, Sikkim, Gujarat, etc. have already taken initiative in this regard.  The pace of computerization and issue
 of Smart Card based driving licenses would ultimately depend upon the Government of respective States/UTs.
 
70.       The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways in respect of
 computerization of Road Transport Sector.  However, the success achieved in the computerization programme leaves
 much to the desired.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways should
 impress upon the States/UTs for expediting both front-end and back-end computerization programme of the road
 transport sectors.  The Ministry should also explore the possibility of providing financial assistance/incentives to the
 States for completing the computerization programme at the earliest.  This would not only help in putting a curb on the
 tampering of licenses by unscrupulous elements but would also ensure the existence of uniform and foolproof system
 for driving licenses by the various states.

71.       A perusal of the Performance Budget 2003-04 of the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways indicates that the

NATIONAL HIGHWAY DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (NHDP)
 
The Committee appreciates that except for a few slippages, the Golden Quadrilateral programme is largely on track and
 is likely to be substantially completed by the targeted period i.e. December 2003. The Committee also expects that the
 projects funded by the World Bank would also be completed by the recommended targeted period, i.e. March 2005.

CENTRAL ROAD FUND (CRF)
 
The Committee in its 59

 utilisation of funds be ensured.  The Committee appreciates that there has been a major improvement in the rate of

 satisfaction that the funds allocated for maintenance and development of National Highways to the States/UTs was
 expected to be fully utilised by them during 2002-03.  The Committee recommends that there should be no let up in the
 measures adopted for the complete utilisation of the funds by the States/UTs and the said trend should continue in the

The Committee is of the view that since the allocation out of the CRF for the State Highways is done by the Ministry of
 Road Transport and Highways, it becomes the responsibility of the Ministry to ensure proper utilisation of the funds.

 mechanism to ensure that the funds released out of the CRF for State Highways are utilised for that purpose only.

 has not only been causing early destruction of several road stretches but also resulting in accidents leading to loss of life
 and property.  The Committee is constrained to note that certain state governments have been regularising overloading
 for financial gains.  The Committee appreciates the States of Karnataka, West Bengal, Meghalaya, Uttar Pradesh,

D R A F T R E P O R T
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/67threport.htm[28-08-2018 13:02:24]
 Tripura and Gujarat for offering tax rebate to popularise the use of multi axle vehicles.  The Committee recommends
 that the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways should further take up the matter with the concerned state
 governments so as to check the problem of overloading. Also the legislation proposed for this purpose should be
 introduced at the earliest.  The Committee also reiterates the recommendations made in its 59th Report that the Ministry
 of Road Transport & Highways should come up with publicity efforts, on large scale, addressing to the truck drivers
 and the agencies engaged in transportation business, including general public.  Themes dealing with dangers of
 overloading should form an important part of the publicity campaigns undertaken in this regard.  Also awareness
 campaigns should be launched including advertisements in print/electronic media. 
(Para 65)
 
COMPUTERISATION OF ROAD TRANSPORT SECTOR
 
The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways in respect of
 computerization of Road Transport Sector.  However, the success achieved in the computerization programme leaves
 much to the desired.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways should
 impress upon the States/UTs for expediting both front-end and back-end computerization programme of the road
 transport sectors.  The Ministry should also explore the possibility of providing financial assistance/incentives to the
 States for completing the computerization programme at the earliest.  This would not only help in putting a curb on the
 tampering of licenses by unscrupulous elements but would also ensure the existence of uniform and foolproof system
 for driving licenses by the various states. 
(Para 70)
 
PERFORMANCE BUDGET
 
A perusal of the Performance Budget 2003-04 of the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways indicates that the
 Performance Budget lacks the information regarding targets/achievements about the specific schemes undertaken by
 the Ministry during the previous year.  In the absence of the above details, the Committee finds it difficult to assess the
 progress of the projects.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Performance Budget should comprise of
 information indicating the targets fixed with specific parameters, actual physical achievements and slippages alongwith
 the reasons for the same.  The physical/financial achievements should be clearly indicated together with the reasons for
 shortfall, if any, in respect of the projects so that the Committee can make proper assessment of the projects executed
 by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways.
(Para 71)

 REPORT
 
            The Department of Culture is the custodian of India’s rich cultural heritage.  In a broader perspective, the
 Department addresses issues relating to national identity in conjunction with several other Ministries and Departments
 such as Tourism, Education, Textiles and External Affairs.  The Department is responsible for promoting art and culture,
 mutual understanding and goodwill and to foster closer relations with foreign countries. Preservation of ancient and
 historic monuments and records, exploration and excavation of archaeological sites and remains, maintenance and
 expansion of libraries, museums of national importance and observance of centenaries and anniversaries of eminent
 personalities are among its other responsibilities.
 
2.         The prime objectives of the Department, i.e. promotion, preservation and conservation of art and culture have been
 implemented under 16 schemes through funding of 26 autonomous organizations and well developed infrastructure of 2
 attached and 6 subordinate offices.
 
3.         The activities and programmes undertaken by the Department of Culture can be broadly classified under the
 following heads:-
 
A.            Archaeology
B.            Museums
C.            Anthropology and Ethnology
D.            Archives & Archival Libraries
E.            Tibetan/Buddhist Studies
F.            Libraries
G.            Akademies & National School of Drama
H.            Promotion and Dissemination of Culture
I.            Memorials
J.            Centenaries & Anniversaries
K.        Cultural Relations & Festival of India
L.            Secretariat
M.        North East Region
 
THE APPROACH IN THE 10
TH PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 2003-04
 
4.         The 10
th Plan has commenced from April 2002.  In the context of 10th Five Year Plan culture has been redefined as
 a vehicle for providing employment opportunities and to spur economic growth apart from strengthening its role as an
 expression of the creative urges of the people.  The focus has also been laid for preservation of Culture at the grass root
 level; implementation of a comprehensive plan for preservation of archeological heritage and development of the
 monument complexes and museums.  The action plan can broadly be summarized as under: -
 (i)         Efforts are to be made for the preservation of the country's archaeological heritage and development of monument
 complexes and museums, besides the archival heritage. Efforts will also be made to promote classical, folk and

 tribal art crafts and oral traditions, which are in danger of dying out.
(ii)        The publication of pending archaeological excavations reports will be expedited.
(iii)            Emphasis must be laid on strengthening inter-organizational networks to introduce a management-oriented
 approach in the administration of cultural institutions. Networking amongst central museums will be strengthened
 enabling these institutions to share their experience and resources in undertaking in-service training, organising
 exhibitions, etc.
 (iv)       Formulation of perspective plans for the important monuments in each circle so as to ensure their integrated
 development.
 (v)        The ASI will strengthen the process of modernisation of galleries, digital documentation of antiquities, publication
 of catalogues, museum guides, picture postcards and other informative material.

 Rs.250.00 crores under Plan. Out of this a sum of Rs.45.00 crores was earmarked for Capital Works and the Capital
 Works Outlay of the Department of Culture is at present being shown in the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Urban
 Development and Poverty Alleviation. This money is spent by the CPWD on the projects of the Department of the Culture
 without taking them into confidence. However, the control over the funds and the pace of progress of the projects (both
 physical and financial) remains with the CPWD due to which progress in number of projects has been tardy e.g. Bhasha
 Bhavan and National Gallery of Modern Art.  The Ministry of Urban Development unilaterally reduced this amount from
 Rs.45.00 crores to Rs.25.51 crores during 2002-03 at R.E. stage.  The Capital Works allocation for the year 2003-04 is

  NATIONAL MISSION FOR MANUSCRIPTS
 
47.            Manuscripts constitute an important segment of our documentary heritage.  India has possibly the oldest and the
 largest collection of manuscripts anywhere in the world. In India millions of manuscripts are available in various
 languages and forms which are custody of different institutions and with individuals, this valuable heritage has not been
 documented or preserved properly. The concern for conservation, preservation and dissemination of this precious
 collection as a living manifestation of our culture has emerged strongly in India in the last few decades.
 
48.       The Committee was informed that the proposed financial outlay for the Mission during the Tenth Five Year Plan is
 estimated to be Rs.35 crores. The Mission is intended to be a systematic effort to document, preserve and disseminate the
 existing collection of Indian manuscripts. The Mission also seeks to locate and identify the manuscripts collections in
 India and abroad through exclusive surveys, document them through descriptive cataloguing, prepare a national database
 and promote their ready access through digitization and publication.
 
49.       During the year 2003-04, Rs. 2 crores has been allocated in BE for the Mission to undertake sensitization and
 awareness building programmes by organizing a number of national and regional level workshops, seminars and training
 programmes, assess the financial requirements of the custodial institutions and extend need based assistance to them,
 document the status of manuscripts in the country and develop a customized software.

 of Culture should identify at least one monuments/sites in each State for inclusion in the list of World Heritage Sites of
 UNESCO and coordinated efforts should be made for integrated infrastructure development conservation/preservation of
 these monuments sites with encompassing facilities for tourists, so as to give a major fillip to cultural tourism in the
 country as well as attracting overseas visitors.
(Paras 21, 24 & 29)
 
ARCHEOLOGICAL CONSERVATION, PRESERVATION AND EVELOPMENT OF MONUMENTS
 
The Committee notes that IOC donated Rs.25 crores to NCF and the amount has been transferred to IOF as Corpus Fund. 
 The Committee is constrained to note that an amount of Rs.10 crores per annum has not been donated by the IOC to the
 NCF for appropriation as per the provisions of MOU.  However, the Department of Culture has sent proposals for
 restorations and conservation of 14 monuments in 10 states to IOC which was later on revised to 25 sites in 25 States. 
 Out of which, initially 5 Heritage monuments/sites has been selected by IOC for Integrated development.    The
 Committee feels that conservation of our rich cultural heritage is important both for encouraging tourism as well as
 attracting overseas visitors. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government should make efforts to procure
 Rs.10 crores from IOC, as decided in the Memorandum of Understanding.  The Committee also recommends the
 Department of Culture to steep up its activities in various sectors and vigorously coordinate efforts with IOC for holistic
 development of these heritage sites/monuments and simultaneously seeks for convergence of resources in coordination
 with other Corporate Sectors/State Governments/Private Sector for development of the rest of the heritage
 sites/monuments in the country.
(Para 37)
ARCHEOLOGICAL EXCAVATION AND EXPLORATION
 
The Committee is not happy with the lackadaisical approach in the matter of publication of pending excavation reports. 
 The Committee notes that reports upto 1996-97 have been published by the ASI but still there remains a backlog for
 writing and printing of these reports.  However, in this connection, the Committee would like to be informed whether the
 final reports on excavation works taken up long back have been finalised as pointed out by the Committee in its
 recommendations contained in its 56
th Report and recommends that the ASI should expedite writing and publication of all
 the pending reports in a time bound manner.
(Para 43)
MUSEUMS
 
The Committee feels that museums are major attractions for tourists, foreign students and scholars and is a link between
 culture and education.  The success of a museum or Art Gallery depends, to a large extent on its ability to project “Unity
 in Diversity’ in the cultural matrix of the nation.  This could be better achieved if an integrated approach has been adopted
 for linking art with science, craft with technology, man made treasures with natural resources and strengthening of basic
 functions of museums in collections, conservation, documentation, research, publication, presentation and education.  The
 Committee recommends the Department of Culture to strengthen and provide better infrastructure to improve the
 standards of museums in the country.  In this connection, the Committee observes that large-scale excavations have been
 undertaken at the sites of Dholavira and Hatab in Gujarat, Govishan, Kashipur in Uttaranchal, Sravasti in UP and Udaigiri
 in Orissa.  The Committee recommends that items found during excavation at Dholavira should be exhibited and
 conserved in a museum at the site itself.
 (Para 46)
NATIONAL MISSION FOR MANUSCRIPTS
 
The Committee recommends that Department of Culture should make consistent efforts and give paramount importance to
 the work relating to preservation of manuscripts and to salvage this cultural heritage from extinction, their preservations
 and continued availability of scholars and public in general.  The Committee also recommends that sincere efforts should
 be initiated to acquire the manuscripts, which are still under private possession partly due to mass ignorance about their
 importance and partly due to attachment towards these as hereditary acquisitions.
(Para 50)

The Committee takes strong exception for reducing the plan allocation of IGNCA from Rs.1 crore in BE 2002-03 to Rs.10
 lakhs in B.E. 2003-04.  The Committee notes that the corpus fund of Rs.50 crores has been increased to Rs.83 crores in
 20002-03 to meet the recurring and non-recurring expenditure and a grant of Rs.100 crores has been released to IGNCA
 for construction activities.  The Committee also notes that the request for enhancement of corpus fund and additional
 amount for its building project is pending before the Cabinet.  However, in this connection the Committee would like to
 reiterate its earlier recommendation contained in 56th Report, which is reproduced below:-
 
“The Committee fails to understand as to how the Centre will be able to manage its recurring expenses from out of
 the accured interest of corpus fund when the rate of interest in changing frequently.  The Committee, therefore,
 recommends that the Government should make an assessment of recurring requirements of the Centre and make
 provision to meet shortage of fund in the budget itself.”
(Para 54)
FESTIVAL OF INDIA
 
The Committee notes that a Festival of India in Bhutan is being organized from March 2003 to October 2003.  The
 Committee does not approve the idea of Department of Culture for reducing the allocation under the head in B.E. 2003-04
 and holding festival of India in foreign countries at a smaller scale to propagate Indian Culture and traditions and
 popularize the rich variety of handicrafts produced in India.   In this connection the Committee would like to draw
 attention of the Government towards its earlier recommendation contained in its 56
th Report wherein the Committee has
 recommended that the Government should chalk out a strategy to make it a regular phenomenon so that the objective of
 promotion of cultural links with foreign countries should be achieved which in turn will also attract the foreign tourists to
 India.
(Para 58)
 
SCIENCE CITIES
 
The Committee is not satisfied with the pace of development work under different science city projects.  The Committee
 feels that the project has been given low priority by the Government, which is reflected by the meagre budgetary
 allocation.  The Committee recommends that Department of Culture should prioritise the projects and provide
 convergence of resources in coordination with State/Private Sector.  The Committee also recommends that Department of
 Culture should explore the possibility of setting up of Science City in each and every State and take into confidence the
 Members of Parliament belonging to respective States so as to ensure coordination and cooperation of local bodies. The
 Government should also see that sufficient funds be provided for these science city projects.
(Para 62)
 
CENTRAL SECRETARIAT LIBRARY & NATIONAL LIBRARY, KOLKATA
 
The Committee is happy to note that sufficient funds have been provided by the Department of Culture during the year
 2003-04 to the modernization of Central and Public Libraries with a view to encourage resource sharing, networking and
 to improve reader services, developing a National Bibliographic Database in electronic format and to carry out activities
 of retro conversion of existing records in electronic formats with National Library and Central Secretariat Library besides
 upgrading of conservation laboratory and construction of reader’s hostel in the National Library.  However, the
 Committee expresses its dismay over slow pace of progress in the construction of Bhasha Bhawan for which no fund has
 been provided this year as informed by the Department of Culture.  The Committee recommends that a time schedule for
 completion of Bhasha Bhawan be prepared and communicated to the Committee and responsibility should also be fixed in
 case of delay, if any, in future.
(Para 72) 
AKADEMIS AND NATIONAL SCHOOL OF DRAMA
 
The Committee notes with satisfaction that Department of Culture has enhanced the plan allocation of Sangeet Natak
 Akademi, Lalit Kala Akademi, Sahitya Akademi and National School of Drama for the year 2003-2004 for continuing its
 on going programmes besides strengthening inter organizational networks to introduced management oriented approach in
 the administration.  The Committee feels that the increased allocation will certainly helps boost these institution to
 achieve their targets. 
(Para 84)
