LALIT KALA AKADEMI
 
The Committee feels that the Lalit Kala Akademi is playing a vital role in the promotion of visual arts in the country.  The
 Committee is in agreement with the suggestion of the Akademi for an increase in the scholarships.  The Committee
 recommends that the number of scholarships in the field of visual and plastic art should be increased from 40 to 64 as
 suggested by the Department of Culture so as to ensure 2 scholarship for each of the 32 States/Union Territories.  It will
 help the Akademi in intending its reach to more and more people as also popularising  the visual and plastic arts.
(Para 89)
 
ZONAL CULTURAL CENTRE
 
The Committee notes that the Zonal Cultural Centres were set with the objective to extend various cultural activities
 specially folk and tribal art forms through them.  The Committee however finds that Zonal Cultural Centres are facing a
 severe resource crunch and consequently very little fund is now available with them for their activities.  The Committee
 recommends that a plan funding should be done for the Zonal Cultural Centres to create additional art infrastructure
 facilities and improve the existing facilities by the Department of Culture besides setting up of uniform facilities across all
 the Zonal Cultural Centres so that activities of Zonal Cultural Centres should be carried out in accordance with the
 objective of promotion and dissemination of the arts of the respective zone.  The Committee also recommends that
 shilpgrams should be setup by all Zonal Cultural Centers for providing promotion and marketing facilities to artisans.
(Para 94)
 
SETTING UP OF MULTI PURPOSE CULTURAL COMPLEXES INCLUDING THOSE FOR CHILDREN
           
The Committee notes that the plan allocation during 2003-2004 has been increased for setting up of Multi Purpose
 Cultural Complexes for Children in coordination with autonomous body created by State Government but still it falls
 short of the requirement of Department of Culture.  As a result, the Department could not take up its proposal for revising
 the guidelines for multipurpose complex.  The Committee is of the view that these complexes will foster and coordinate
 activities in the State in the different cultural field such as music, drama, dance, literature, fine arts etc. and promote the
 cultural unity of the country.   The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government of India should provide
 sufficient outlay for timely completion of Multi Purpose Cultural Complexes and to enable the Department of Culture to
 take up the work of revision of guidelines of the scheme.
(Para 101)
 
NORTH EAST REGION
 
The Committee is happy to note that the Department of Culture has been able to utilize 100 per cent plan outlay allocated
 for North East Region during 2002-2003 to highlight and popularize the rich and diverse art and culture of North East
 India including Sikkim.  The Committee notes that a budgetary allocation of Rs.22 crores has been made during 2003-
2004 for various activities and programme of the Department of Culture in North East Region.  The Committee
 recommends that the Department of Culture should adopt proactive approach in initiating activities so that rich cultural
 wealth of North Eastern Region will come into limelight.
(Para 104)
 
 
 
COORDINATION BETWEEN THE DEPARTMENT OF TOURISM AND DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE 
 
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department of Culture and Department of Tourism should develop some
 institutional mechanism with regard to the formulation of policies and projects for integrated development, conservation
 and preservations of monuments. Coordinated efforts should be taken by the Department of Culture in consultation with
 the Department of Tourism in order to ensure integrated development of clusters of monuments.
(Para 106)

INTRODUCTION
 
            The Ministry of Civil Aviation is responsible for the formulation and implementation of national policies and
 programmes in the civil aviation sector.  The Ministry oversees the development and regulation of civil aviation in the
 country including inter-alia establishment of new aerodromes, maintenance and upgradation of the existing aerodromes,

RATIONALISATION OF SALES TAX ON AIR TURBINE FUEL
 
53.       Fuel is the largest component of airline cost.  The domestic air transport industry in India has been facing serious
 problems due to high cost of operations for which one of the major reasons is the heavy cost of Air Turbine Fuel
 (ATF).  Even though the pricing of ATF is now on import parity basis, the rates applicable for domestic operations
 continue to be significantly higher than that of international operations.  The cost of ATF goes up even further due to
 high rates of sales tax levied by the State Governments/Union Territory administration varying from 20 per cent to 36
 per cent which affects the viability of domestic airline operations.  The Committee observed that both Indian Airlines
 and Air India had cited the high cost of ATF as one of the major factors for increase in expenditure.  During the course
 of his evidence, Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation commented as under:-
 
“…. So far, we have not got the relief which we wanted to have with regard to the ATF.  Apart from the high price
 charged by the oil companies, there are two components.  One is the excise duty which is charged by the Government
 of India and the other is the sales tax, levied by various States.  In Kerala, in spite of the fact that sales tax on ATF has
 been reduced from 39 per cent to 25 per cent, a large amount on account of sales tax is incurred by the airlines…. ”
 
54.       The Committee was also informed by the Ministry of Civil Aviation that the Minister of Civil Aviation had
 written to all the Chief Ministers to consider an appropriate reduction in the rate of sales tax on ATF in the states. 
 Further, the Committee was informed that State Government of Andhra Pradesh has reduced the sales tax on ATF to 4
 per cent and the State Government of Karnataka had committed to reduce the same. 
 
55.       Fuel plays a crucial role in the cost structure and profitability of any airline.  The Committee is of the view that
 the high cost of ATF for domestic air transport increases the cost of operation and makes it unviable even in areas
 where it has comparative advantage over other modes of transport.  The Committee appreciates the initiative taken by
 the State Government of Andhra Pradesh in reducing the rate of sales tax on ATF to 4 per cent.  The Committee hopes
 that this step of the Government of Andhra Pradesh would encourage the other State Governments to follow suit.  The
 Committee recommends that Ministry of Civil Aviation should impress upon the State Governments to come forward
 and reduce the sales tax on AFT to the minimum level, preferably 4 per cent.
 
56.       The Committee has also been informed that some of the states are of the view that there is not much by way of
 airport infrastructure or flight availability in their states and hence, they would not like to lose revenue by reducing rate
 of sales tax on ATF.  In this context, the Committee recommends that the Ministry of Civil Aviation should take up the
 matter with the State Governments with respect to the requirements of air connectivity etc. for their states and try to
 evolve a solution whereby decision on all these problems could be taken as a package deal.

SCHEDULE OF VARIOUS DOMESTIC AIRLINES
 
70.       The Committee also drew the attention of the Ministry of Civil Aviation to the fact there are a number of flights,
 both Indian Airlines and private airlines, operating between different stations, both in the morning as well as in the
 evening.  Also, there is very little difference in the schedule of Indian Airlines and the private airlines.  However, there
 were not many flights during the intervening period of the day.  Many Members of the Committee also stated that there
 was a general impression that prime time flights on various sectors are being given to private operators where Indian
 Airlines could have operated its own flights and cited instances in support of their apprehension.  The Committee then
 enquired about the procedure followed for approval of schedule of various domestic airlines. 
 
71.       In reply the Ministry of Civil Aviation informed that in accordance with the International practice, DGCA is
 approving two flight schedules in a year, namely, winter schedule effective from Monday of the last week of October
 and summer schedule effective from Monday of last week of March.  All domestic scheduled operators file their
 proposed flight schedule in the prescribed application form 45 days before the commencement of the schedule.  After
 receipt of the proposed flight schedule from all operators, a combined airport movement report in respect of all
 operators from all airports is generated within a week at DGCA. It is ensured by DGCA that flight schedules of the
 operators meet the Route Dispersal Guidelines of Ministry of Civil Aviation.  The combined airport movement report is
 forwarded to various concerned agencies like Airports Authority of India, Air Headquarters, Naval Headquarters, HAL,
 Bangalore, Cochin International Airport Ltd for time slot approval and also to Bureau of Civil Aviation Security for
 security clearance.  The combined airport movement report is also forwarded to all scheduled operators.

72.       Airports Authority of India convenes a meeting about 3 weeks before the commencement of the schedule with
 all operators and all concerned agencies to discuss the flight schedule and allocation of time slots desired by the
 operators.  A revised airport movement report is then generated by DGCA incorporating all the changes in the time
 slots and sent to all concerned agencies for their approval.  The flight schedules of all operators are finally approved by
 DGCA based on the approvals received from various concerned agencies 15 days before the commencement of the
 schedule. 
 
73.       The schedule is the primary product attribute in the airline business.   The inherent nature of domestic market is
 such that demand, on most routes, tends to be concentrated around peak periods, and all airlines, therefore, tend to fix
 their timings during this peak period in order to be able to attract maximum number of passengers.   For this reason
 flight timing of airlines tend to be close to each other.   For example, on major metros mornings and evenings are the
 preferred time slots for all airlines operating on the route.  The process of approval of the schedules has to be such as to
 avoid allegations of lack of transparency and motivated fixation of timings.
 
74.       Although Ministry of Civil Aviation have stated in their reply that the process of approval of the schedules has to
 be such as to avoid allegations of lack of transparency and motivated fixation of timings, the Committee is constrained
 to note that prime timings are being given to the private airlines and Indian Airlines operates its flights at odd hours
 which not only results in inconvenience to the passengers but also most of the passengers load is diverted towards
 private airlines.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that this issue should be seriously looked into and flight
 timings of Indian Airlines flights should be rescheduled for better utilisation of its seat capacity.  The Committee also
 recommends that there should be coordination between the Indian Airlines and the private airlines at the time of
 finalisation of their schedule so that there is a staggering of the multiple flights existing at peak hours which would
 result in improved air services to the passengers during the non-peak hours also.

DEVELOPMENT OF INTERMEDIATE AND MINOR PORTS
 
20.       There are 184 minor/intermediate ports located along the coastline of India.  Most of these are located in
 Maharashtra, Gujarat, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. The Minor Ports are under the administrative domain
 of the State Governments who are also responsible for their development and creating capacities at their ports. 
 However, only 53 minor ports are well developed and provide all weather berthing facilities for cargo handling.  The
 remaining ports cater to fishing boats, passenger boats etc.  The cargo handled by these ports comprises mainly fishery
 products, food grains, fertilisers, building materials, coal, cement, petroleum crude and petro-products and edible oil. 
21.       The traffic handled by minor ports is continuously on the rise, increasing from 27.83 mt in 1996-97 to 86.58 mt
 in 2000-01. Currently, nearly 25 per cent of the total traffic is being handled by the intermediate/minor ports. 
22.       On a question of increasing the capacity of the minor ports in the country, Ministry of Shipping informed that
 the major ports fall within the ambit of the Central Government, while the responsibility for the development of non-
major ports lie with respective State Governments.  However, the Ministry of Shipping has decided to get a study
 conducted for development of coastal shipping and minor ports.  The study has been given to a consultant who will
 submit a report within this calendar year.  After receipt of the Report, Government will finalise its stand on the
 recommendations of the study.  The Ministry of Shipping also has a scheme for grant of Central Assistance to the
 Maritime States for conducting feasibility/environmental/hydrographic studies etc. for development of minor ports. 
 The total capacity of all ports in the country is sufficient to handle the present cargo.
 
23.       The Committee notes that the minor ports serve not only as trans-shipment points for trade but also as catalysts
 for economic activities in their respective regions. The role of minor ports is becoming increasingly important owing to
 the development of coastal shipping and they should be viewed as an alternative to congested major ports.  The
 Committee recommends that Ministry of Shipping should impress upon the concerned States to provide adequate funds
 for the development of minor ports so that they could effectively cater to coastal vessels and assist in development of
 the hinterland.  The Committee also recommends that keeping in view the contribution and importance of minor ports
 in cargo handling, Government of India may also consider to provide central grants to the Maritime States for
 development of Minor Ports.

 Further, no pensioner so far has been paid the arrears arising out of revision of their pension. Apart from this, by virtue
 of the amendment of the Gratuity Act, 1972 with effect from 24.9.1997, gratuity at the enhanced rate i.e. Rs. 3.5 lakhs
 maximum, is payable to 540 retirees. The arrear payment for commutation pension payable at enhanced rate i.e. 40
 percent has also not been made so far.  For the employees and workers retired from 1.1.2002, it has not been possible to
 make payment on account of encashment of earned leave on superannuation.
 
28.       To overcome the situation various steps have already been taken by the Board to reduce the expenditure and to
 generate revenue. The Board has also undertaken cost cutting measures to reduce expenditure to the extent possible.
 Board is also identifying assets that are lying idle for disposal to augment its financial position. The Board has also
 considered necessary to introduce a special VRS for about 790 employees and workers to downsize the strength to a
 manageable figure.  For this purpose a proposal for grant of Rs.52.00. crores has been received from the Board and is
 under examination in consultation with the Ministry of Finance.  Further, Chairman, CDLB has also requested
 Government to consider providing one time grant of Rs.43.00 crores to the Board for the purpose of payment of
 outstanding dues to pensioners of the Board. The proposal has been examined in consultation with the Finance Wing of
 the Ministry and the same has been recommended to Ministry of Finance for consideration.
 
29.       The Committee takes strong exception to the fact that CDLB has not implemented revision of pension and
 liberlisation of post retirement benefits in terms of wage settlement and the pensioners/retired employees have not been
 paid pension and other post retirement benefits including gratuity, PF settlement etc. for the past so many months. The
 Committee feels that pensioners after their retirement fully depends on their retirement benefits and if the same are not
 disbursed to them in time, it will lead to harassment and it is also against the law.  The Committee does not approve the
 lackadaisical approach of the Ministry of Shipping in sharing the responsibility of pensioners of CDLB.  The
 Committee recommends that Ministry of Shipping should take responsibility in the matter and ensure that payment of
 pensionary benefits to the employee of CDLB who retired prior to 1.1.98 and revision on pension and payment of
 arrears etc. be implemented at the earliest.

 According to a study, the liner cargo traffic at the Indian ports would increase from a level of 45.31 MT in 1996-97 to
 about 118.62 MMT in 2006-07 showing a compound growth of about 10percent per annum.
 
72.       The Committee enquired from the Ministry the efforts taken by the them to arrest the current decline in Indian
 tonnage and fate of the introduction of tonnage tax in lieu of Corporate Tax.  The Ministry of Shipping informed that
 the Cabinet Secretariat, while conveying approval of Cabinet Committee on Security to the proposal of this Ministry on
 “Para 5.52 of the recommendations of the Group of Ministers on Reforming the National Security System – Policy for
 Maritime Shipbuilding” has directed the Ministry of Shipping to discuss and finalise the modalities of the proposed
 fiscal regime with Ministry of Finance & Company Affairs.

73.            Subsequently, a six members committee comprising of two members each from Ministry of Shipping, CBDT
 and Indian National Shipowners’ Association was formed to finalise the modalities of the proposed fiscal regime and
 try to structure the required legislation regarding tonnage tax.  The Committee has discussed the draft legislation for
 introduction to Tonnage Tax for the Shipping industry.  However, a final decision on the introduction of tonnage tax
 has yet to be taken. 
 
74.       The Ministry has further informed that the Government has been taking various steps from time to time to
 modernise and diversifies the fleet of India Shipping Industry.  The following steps for development and giving
 necessary boost to the Shipping sector have so far been taken by the Government: -
 
              I.      Shipping companies have been allowed to retain sale proceeds of their ships abroad and utilise them for fresh
 acquisition;
           II.      No permission is required for raising foreign exchange loans from abroad by mortgaging the vessel with the
 lender;
         III.      100 percent Foreign Direct Investment in Shipping Sector is permitted;
        IV.      Section 33 AC of Income Tax has been restored in its original form, thereby facilitating plough back of profits
 by shipping Companies for new acquisition;
           V.      The provisions of “EXIM POLICY” relating to import of vessels has been amended w.e.f. 1.4.2001 bringing all
 categories of vessels/ships under OGL and thereby dispensing with licence requirement for import of various
 kinds ships.  Ships could now be imported freely without licence;
        VI.      The Depreciation rate on ships has been enchanced from 20 percent to 25 percent w.e.f. 1.4.2001, thereby
 facilitating faster tonnage replacement;
 
75.            Ministry of Shipping has taken several measures to encourage the growth of Indian Shipping Industry.  To
 facilitate tonnage growth, the Ministry has also taken several proactive steps, viz., and simplification of guidelines for
 import of ships, doing away with age norms etc.  In spite of these efforts only 6.82 million GT has achieved as on
 31.03.2002.  During 10
th Plan, the priority is to remove the constraints with a view to achieve an addition of 3.26
 million gross Tonnage (GT) by acquisition of 156 vessels of various categories by creating a conducive environment
 for raising of external borrowings. The Secretary, Ministry of shipping in his deposition also stated: -
“One of the reasons for this slow-down in the shipping trade is the absence of a facilitative fiscal environment. 
 The size of the fleet needs to be increased and for this we need to have tonnage tax.  This is important because
 the shipping industry does not compete within the country alone on an average the world’s fleet pays nominal
 tax of about 2 to 3 percent.  Our shipping companies pay tax at about 30 to 35 percent.  We had a committee
 under the Chairmanship of Shri Rakesh Mohan, which recommended the implementation of tonnage tax.  But
 for some reason or the other, this tax has not been introduced.  Unless this is done, it is not possible to increase
 the size of the fleet.  In India, we spend an estimated ten- percent of our total foreign trade by way of freight. 
 Last year, foreign trade stood at 96 billion dollars.  Even if we take only 75 percent of that value as that
 passing through ports, we are looking at 7.2 billion dollars. It comes to about Rs. 35,500 crores.  If we were
 like other developed countries, our freight charges would come down to Rs. 27,600 crores, a fall of nearly Rs.
 8000 crores.  For this reason, it is very important to have a large fleet.  It is important for other reasons also.  It
 will give a boost to businesses like ship booking, insurance, maritime law, chandlering, ship management,
 manning agencies, etc.  Also, this will provide employment opportunities.  In the U.K., tonnage tax was
 introduced in the year 1998.  Invisibles increased in the U.K. economy by two billion pounds Two billion
 pounds are equal to approximately Rs.14,000 crores, which is a huge amount.  This was the amount of benefit
 that economy was able to get.  We believe that the same thing should happen here.  If reforms could be
 brought about, a lot of things could happen to the Indian fleet.  Not only invisibles will go up, but employment
 will also go up.”

 proposal on the ground that in the event of setting up of the SBM by the KRL in the open sea, there would be non-
utilisation of the existing infrastructure created by the port exclusively for the Kochi Refineries Ltd. (KRL) for handling

2003 respectively of the Ministry of Shipping recommended that Ministries of Shipping and Petroleum and Natural Gas
 to evolve an amicable solution to the problem. Kochi Refinery Ltd. should consider, in the national interest, the
 alternative proposals suggested by the Cochin Port Trust before taking up the construction of the Single Buoy Mooring.

 Committee on the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial (Amendment) Bill, 2003*.

th April 2003.  In pursuance of rules relating to the
 Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committees, the Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha, in consultation with the

 meeting held on the 5

 provisions of the Bill pertaining to the appointment/nomination of the Trustees and several other important issues.

th September
 2003.  The Committee considered the draft Report on the subject in its meeting held on the 16th October 2003 and
 adopted the same with Notes of dissent from some Members.

 Shri K. Rahman Khan jointly and from Shri G.M. Banatwalla and Shri Vilas Muttemwar separately, may be appended
 to the report.

 assistance provided during deliberations on the provisions of the Bill.

REPORT
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre, which took place on the 13th day of April 1919, was the
 defining moment in the country’s struggle for independence.  It symbolised the national resolve to
 protest against the ruthless cruelty of the colonial power.  It has got immense historical importance
 and strong sentiment of millions of people of this country is attached with this place.  In order to
 provide for erection and management of a National Memorial to perpetuate the memory of those

 Bagh National Memorial Act, (Annexure-I) was passed by the Parliament in 1951. A Trust was
 constituted under this Act to look after the functions, maintenance and development of the
 Memorial.  With the passage of time three life trustees passed away and these seats remained vacant
 since new members were not appointed.  Amendment in the abovesaid Act was necessary to fill up

 (Annexure-II) has been brought forward.  At the same time, it also seeks through this 
 legislation to form the Committee of Management to look after the Trust’s affairs on a day-to-day
 basis.
2.       The Statement of Objects and Reasons of the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial
 (Amendment) Bill, 2003 inter-alia states the following points:
2.1     The object of the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial Act, 1951 was to place the then existing
 Trust on a permanent basis, to establish a body corporate to be known as the Trustees of the
 Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial, to transfer to that body all the property and funds to confer
 upon that body all necessary powers for carrying out the objects of the Trust.
2.2     It further states that the Trust has also got responsibility for erection and maintenance of
 buildings, structures and parks at or near the site of the Jallianwala Bagh in the city of Amritsar.  It
 has to be done by acquiring lands, buildings and other properties for the purposes of the Trust and
 raising and receiving funds for the purposes of the National Memorial.
2.3     Over a period of time, the Trustees for life passed away and the Government does not have
 proper representation on the Trust.  Further, The Government cannot appoint Trustees for life
 without making necessary amendments in the said Act.  Therefore, with a view to filling up the
 vacancies caused on account of passing away of the life Trustees, it has become necessary to amend
 the said Act through the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial (Amendment) Bill, 2003.
2.4     Jallianwala Bagh is a National Memorial revered by all the Indians.  The new composition
 proposed in the Bill would make the Trust much more representative in its character.  The Trust will
 receive the rightful recognition and importance if it is headed by the Prime Minister as proposed.
3.       In  paragraph (3) of the Statement of Objects and Reasons, the Ministry has submitted
 that this legislation has been brought forward in view to filling up the vacancies caused on

 of the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial Trust as prescribed in the parent Act was in order
 and the inclusion of the President of the Indian National Congress was in keeping with the
 contribution of the Indian National Congress in the freedom movement in general, and
 glorious struggle which led to the Jallianwala Bagh incident in particular.  The intention of the
 present Bill can be in no way to belittle the contribution of the Indian National Congress in the
 freedom movement.  The Committee therefore, recommends that this intention should be
 clearly reflected in the Aims and Objectives of the Bill.  The Committee also observes that
 through this Bill, the entire administrative structure of the Trust as well as the Committee of
 Management would undergo major changes.  However, the Statement of Objects and Reasons
 of the Bill doesn’t reflect the actual changes to be brought through the proposed legislation.   
 The Committee therefore, recommends that a comprehensive Statement of Objects and
 Reasons is required to be drafted taking into account all the changes proposed to be carried in
 the composition of the Trust as well as the Committee of Management.
4.       In their background note (Annexure-III) furnished to the Committee giving the reasons for the
 introduction of the Bill, the Department of Culture has brought out the following points:
4.1     As per the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial Act, 1951, the
 composition of the Trust was as follows:
(a)      Shri Jawaharlal Nehru,
(b)     Shri Saifuddin Kitchlew,
(c)     Shri Maulana Abul Kalam Azad,
(d)     The President of the Indian National Congress,
(e)      The Governor of the State of Punjab,
(f)      The Chief Minister of the State of Punjab and
(g)     Three persons to be nominated by the Central Government
5.     Since, the life members of the Trust from (a) to (c) mentioned above have passed away, these
 seats have to be filled up and it can be done only through amendments of the said Act by the
 Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial (Amendment) Bill, 2003.

7.       During the course of evidence, the Secretary, Department of Culture inter-alia  submitted that
 there was no provision in the Act to appoint the Trustees in place of those life members who died
 and those seats are still vacant. It was realised from time to time that there was need for amending in
 the above said Act. There was a meeting with the Secretary to the Prime Minister in 1979 and it was
 their observation that the present Act should be amended.  According to these observations, this Bill
 has been prepared.  He further added that at early stage, there was lack of fund in the Trust and after
 1981, no donation was received from States for the purpose of this Memorial.  Rupees two cores and
 fifty lakhs were sanctioned in the year 1998 by the Central Government and out of which Rupees
 two crores were released to the Trust.
8.       The Committee feels that the Ministry has treated this Trust of esteemed national
 importance in a very negligent manner.  Though the need for amendment in the Act was
 realised twenty-four years back there was an inordinate delay on the part of Ministry in
 bringing out the required legislation.  The reasons cited for such delay were not very
 convincing and after going through the details, the Committee realises that due to this
 negligent attitude and with an almost defunct Trust assets/properties of the Memorial could
 not be utilised properly.  The Committee therefore, hopes that Government will do away with
 this kind of lackadaisical approach in future and after the Bill is passed by the Parliament
 necessary Rules/Regulations will be framed and the vacancies in the trust will be filled up to
 make the Trust functional expeditiously.

2.         The Committee took-up clause-by-clause consideration of the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial
 (Amendment) Bill, 2003.
2.1
              In respect of Clause 2(1) (d), some members mentioned that the proposed Bill does not include the President of
 the Indian National Congress as was in Section 4(1) (d) of the parent Act, namely the Jallianwala Bagh National
 Memorial Act 1951.  The exclusion of the President of the Indian National Congress was not acceptable to them as
 such a move would tantamount to ignoring the entire contribution of the Indian National Congress in the freedom
 struggle of the country.
2.2              However, some other members while recognising the valuable contribution made by the Indian National
 Congress in the freedom struggle of the country felt that over the years several changes and other development have
 taken place and therefore, felt that it was no longer necessary to have the President of Indian National Congress in the
 proposed amendment Bill. This group of members therefore, suggested that inclusion of the President of the Indian
 National Congress should not be insisted upon.  They, therefore, were of the view that the amendment of the parent Act
 as proposed, should be passed. 
2.3              Section 2 (1) (h) envisages that Secretary to Govt. of India in the Department of Culture as Member-Secretary to
 the Trust, ex-officio.  The Committee considered this provision in the Bill and felt that it was not correct for the
 Secretary to the Department to be included as Member-Secretary to the Trust.  He should serve only as Secretary to the
 Trust.
2.4.      As regards Statement of Objects and Reasons, the Committee recommended that the Statement of Objects and
 Reasons should be amended to reflect the true picture of the proposed legislation.
2.5.      As regards Section 2(1) (c) of Clause 2, the Committee observed that there is no justification given by the
 Department of Culture for having the Union Minister of Home Affairs as a member of the Trust.  The maintenance of
 the Memorial and looking after the freedom fighters and their families are different functions.  The Committee found
 no       co-relation between the functioning of the Trust and role of Home Minister as a Member in the Trust.  Therefore,
 the Committee recommended that Clause 2 (1) (c) may be deleted.
2.6.      As regards to Section 2 (1) (g) of Clause 2, the Committee noted that the criteria for nominating the ‘eminent
 persons’ has not been given in the Bill.  The Committee, therefore, recommended that those criteria should be provided
 in the Bill itself.

INTRODUCTION
         I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism & Culture,
 having been authorised by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby present this Seventy-second Report of the
 Committee on the Action Taken by the Government on the recommendations/observations contained in its Sixtieth
 Report on Development of Tourism in the Country.
2.      The Sixtieth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and
 Culture was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 21
st November 2002.
 
3.      Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained in its Sixtieth Report were received
 from the Department of Tourism on 5th March 2003.
 
4.      The Committee considered the subject and adopted the Report in its meeting held on 29th October 2003.
 
NEW DELHI      
October 29, 2003
Kartika 7, 1925 (Saka)                                    
NILOTPAL BASU
 Chairman,
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
 Transport, Tourism & Culture.
R E P O R T
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the observations/
 recommendations as contained in its Sixtieth Report on Development of Tourism in the Country, which was presented,
 to the Parliament on 21st November 2002.
2.         Action Taken Replies have been received from the Government on 5 th March 2003 in respect of all the
 observations/recommendations contained in the Report, which have been categorised as follows:-
(i)         Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Government:
              Nil                                                                                                      Total-0
(ii)        Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue             in view of the
 Government replies:
Para Nos.: 11,13                                                                                  Total-2
(iii)       Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government   have not been accepted by the
 Committee:
Para Nos.:  20                                                                                      Total-1
(iv)       Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the    Government are still awaited:
Para Nos.: 8,19,24,26,28,30,32                                                              Total-7
3.         The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which have been categorized
 as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest.
4.         On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee  has made observations on each item of Action
 taken/proposed to be taken by the Department.  The recommendations of the Committee contained in the Sixtieth
 Report, action taken thereon by the Government, and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of
 action taken has been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
 
SINGLE WINDOW CLEARANCE SYSTEM
RECOMMENDATION (Para 8)

5.         The Committee had, in its 48 th Report on the Demands for Grants (2001-2002) of the Department of Tourism,
 expressed the view that the Government, through its own limited resources, has not been able to provide the requisite
 funds for the development of tourist infrastructure in the country.  Accordingly, the Committee had recommended for
 early implementation of the Single Window Clearance System.  The Committee is of the opinion that the participation
 of the private sector can go a long way in supplementing the efforts of the Government in developing the tourist
 infrastructure in the country and the private sector takes into consideration long-term perspective in facilities required
 therefor.  The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Central/State/UT Governments must try to remove
 the obstacles faced by the private investors and ensure early implementation of the Single Window Clearance System
 for tourism projects. 
 
Reply of the Government
 
6.         The Department of Tourism is committed towards the development of tourism infrastructure in the country and
 encourages participation of the private sector in supplementing the efforts of the Government in their endeavour for
 developing tourist infrastructure of international standards.  From time to time, the Department of Tourism has taken up
 the issue with the State/UT Governments to facilitate the private investor by the way of reducing/removing the hassles
 in obtaining various clearances/NOCs by implementing a Single Window Clearance System.  Accordingly, the
 Department had sent a communication in March 2001 to all the State/UTs regarding the Single Window Clearance
 facility for tourism projects.  In response the Government of West Bengal has stated that such arrangement has not been
 provided in their State.  Again in April and November, 2002 all the State Governments/UTs have been reminded to
 create Single Window System for clearance of the projects pending with the State instead of multi-agencies.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
7.         The Committee recommends that the Department of Tourism should take up the matter with all the
 States/UTs for implementation of the Single window Clearance System for tourism projects so as to remove the
 hurdles faced by the private investors in development of the tourist infrastructure in the Country.  The
 Committee notes the efforts made by the Department of Tourism towards development of tourism in the country
 and participation of the Private Sector in Development of Tourism infrastructure of international standards.
 
LACK OF VISA-ON-ARRIVAL SCHEME
RECOMMENDATION (Para 11)
 
8.         The Committee agrees that the security considerations of the country cannot be compromised.  However, it must
 also be admitted that granting visa-on-arrival to the foreign tourists at the airports can certainly give a boost to the
 foreign tourist arrivals in the country.  The Committee is of the view that a step in this direction can be taken by
 initially introducing visa-on-arrival for tourists from friendly countries, countries which do not pose a security threat to
 our country and are tourism generating markets.  Later, if the scheme is successful and helps in foreign tourist influx to
 the country, it can be extended to other countries too on a case-to-case basis.
 
Reply of the Government
 
9.         The Ministry of Home Affairs have informed that the scheme of visa-on-Arrival cannot be accepted due to
 current security scenario prevailing in the country.
 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
10.       The Committee notes the reply of the Government.
 
 
SPECIAL TOURIST POLICE FORCE

RECOMMENDATION (Para 13)
 
11.       The Committee feels that the issue relating to the safety and security of the tourists, especially foreign tourists is
 very important and needs to be looked into seriously.  The Committee is of the view that incidents of harassment of
 foreign tourists bring a bad name to the country and have an adverse effect on the foreign tourist arrival.  Deployment
 of Special Tourism Police Force can be an effective tool for ensuring safety and security of the tourists.  The
 Committee appreciates the creation of the Special Tourism Police Force by some of the states.  The Committee also
 suggests that the police personnel of the States should also be provided special 'tourist-oriented' training.  Such form of
 official protection to international and domestic tourists would certainly instil confidence amongst the tourists visiting
 these territories.  A successful implementation of such measures will definitely encourage the other State Governments
 in implementing similar schemes for the promotion of tourism in their respective States.
 
Reply of the Government
 
12.       The Governments of Kerala, J&K, Rajasthan, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh have
 set-up Tourist Police Force for the safety and security of the foreign tourists.
 
13.       Government of Delhi, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Chandigarh are in the process of setting
 up of Tourist Police Force.
 
14.       Some of the States/UTs e.g. Mizoram, Daman & Diu, Assam, Sikkim, Pondicherry, Lakshadweep have not felt
 the necessity of the Tourist Police Force and have instructed the regular police force to look into safety and security of
 the foreign tourists.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
15.       The Committee notes the reply of the Government.
 
RATIONALISATION OF TAXES ON THE TOURISM INDUSTRY
RECOMMENDATION (Para 19)  
 
16.       The Committee feels that the hotel industry is the backbone of tourism.  The major share of tourism revenue to
 the government is contributed by this sector.  However, there are a lot of taxes and sometimes duplication of taxes at
 both Central and State levels on the hotel sector.  The multiple taxes have imposed a heavy financial burden on the
 hotel industry.  The Committee observes that taxes on hotel rooms and food levied by both the Centre and the States
 add upto over 45 percent, making the industry grossly uncompetitive.  The Committee is of the view that there ought to
 be coordination and synergy between the Centre and the State Governments on the tax front and that there is an urgent
 need to rationalize both Central and State taxes on tourism.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Central
 Government/State Governments must come forward with rationalisation of taxes and provide concessions for the hotel
 industry to give a fillip to the arrival of the tourists in the States.  Further there should be uniformity in the rate of
 various taxes levied by the State Governments on the hotel industry.
 
Reply of the Government
 
17.       The Department of Tourism has been taking steps for the rationalization of taxes levied by the Central
 Government and the State Governments. 
 
18.       Several taxes on the hotel industry like Luxury Tax and Sales Tax are levied by the State Governments.  These
 taxes coupled with the Expenditure Tax levied by the Central Govt. impose a heavy burden on the hotel industry, which
 is passed on to the occupants, thereby increasing the cost of accommodation.
 
19.       In the meeting of Chief Ministers and Tourism Ministers of all States held on 30.10.2001, the State Governments
 were requested to rationalise these taxes.  Again in a meeting held on 5.9.2002 of all the Tourism Ministers and the
 tourism Secretaries, this issue was again taken up with the State Governments.

20.       As regards the levies of the Central Governments, the issue was taken up with the Ministry of Finance in the
 Department of Tourism’s Pre-budget Memorandum for the year 2002-03.  As a result following measures were
 announced in the Budget 2002-03:-
 
Expenditure Tax:
Expenditure Tax on hotels to apply only to room charges henceforth: earlier expenditure tax was charged
 on room charges as well as other services. Threshold of Rs.2000 raised to Rs.3000 for levy of
 expenditure tax.
 
Service Tax:
Service Tax exemption given earlier to be extended for one more year; in  case of functions and banquets
 where the entire bill is for catering services, no service tax would be charged.
 
80HHC and 80 HHD:
Disparities between 80HHC AND 80 HHD removed.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
21.       The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Department of Tourism towards rationalisation of
 taxes levied by the Central Government and State Government.  The Committee also appreciates the measures
 announced by the Government in the Budget 2002-03 though State Governments have not yet taken any decision
 on rationalisation of taxes.  The Committee recommends that Department of Tourism should pursue the State
 Governments for rationalisation of different taxes and provide incentives for the hotel Industry so as to boost
 this Industry at large and to generate tourist arrivals.
 
RATIONALISATION OF TAXES ON THE TOURISM INDUSTRY
RECOMMENDATION (Para 20)
 
22.       The Committee observes that there is a lack of uniformity in taxes, laws and regulation across the States.  While
 the State Governments are taking steps to develop tourism in their respective states, the lack of coordination among
 them and the higher rates of road tax/disparity in the taxes in the states, especially southern States have had negative
 effect on the growth of tourism in these states.  These factors also result in hardships for the tourists as also increase the
 cost of travel for the tourists.  The Committee therefore, recommends that there should be a composite transport permit
 for tourist vehicles.  The Committee also recommends that the Central and the State Governments should take
 immediate steps to create uniformity between the local vehicles and the visiting vehicles.  Steps should also be taken to
 facilitate easy travel and free inter-State movement for tourist vehicles.
 
Reply of the Government
 
23.       As regards the taxes on the travel sector, these taxes are levied by the respective State Governments.  Not only
 are the rates of these levies are very high, but even the mode of levy varies from State to State.
 
24.       The Department of tourism took up this matter with the State Government. in the Tourism Minister’s
 Conference.
 
25.       The matter was also taken up with the Ministry of Highways and Road Transport.  They had included this
 subject as an agenda in the Transport Development Council attended by the Transport Ministers and the Transport
 Secretaries of the State Governments.  Though this matter was discussed a consensus could not be arrived at to resolve
 the issue.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE

26.       The Committee understands the compulsions of the Department of Tourism in enforcing the composite
 transport permit for tourism vehicles.  The Committee, however, recommends that Department of Tourism
 should keep pursuing the State Governments for bringing uniformity in taxes, laws and regulation for reduction
 of road taxes etc. to facilitate easy travel and free inter-state movement of tourist vehicles.    
 
TOURISM DEVELOPMENT IN ANDAMAN & NICOBAR AND LAKSHADWEEP ISLANDS
 
RECOMMENDATION (Para 24)
 
27.       The Committee feels that Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands have the potential of growing into top
 destinations for beach tourism and water sports.  But for the constraint of transportation of tourists from the mainland,
 these islands would have attracted a still larger number of tourists, earning revenue and generating employment for the
 local islanders.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the work on the extension of runway at Port Blair may be
 completed at the earliest and the frequency of flights may also be increased so that more and more tourists are able to
 land there.  The Committee welcomes the decision of DGCA to permit the foreign tourist charter flights to land at Port
 Blair and recommends that this fact may be given wide publicity amongst national as well as international tour
 operators.  Similarly, round the year air services, well connected with other important centres like Kochi,
 Thiruvananthapuram and Goa may be introduced to give a boost to the development and promotion of tourism in the
 Lakshadweep Islands. Further, clearance to the proposals for construction of airfields at Kavarati, Minicoy, Andrott,
 Kadmat and Kiltan Islands should be expedited.  The Committee also feels that creating eco-friendly tourist
 infrastructure and water sports facility involves huge expenditure.  Due to the limited resources available to these two
 Union Territories, it may not be possible for the administration of these islands to create infrastructure and other
 facilities in the islands.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the administration of these islands should create
 conducive atmosphere for private investment and, thereafter, invite private sector participation in developing the
 necessary infrastructure, accommodation and high quality eco-friendly tourists/resorts.
 
Reply of the Government
 
28.       The Administrator of A&N Islands and Lakshadweep Islands/DGCA have been requested to develop
 infrastructure for the promotion of tourism and for creation of conducive atmosphere for private investment and invite
 private sector participation in developing the necessary infrastructure, accommodation and high quality eco-friendly
 tourist resorts but no reply has been received from the above mentioned departments.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
29.       The Committee notes the reply and recommends that the Department of Tourism should keep pursuing
 the matter vigorously with the administration of A&N Islands and Lakshadweep Islands.
 
PERMIT SYSTEM FOR THE TOURISTS
RECOMMENDATION (Paras 26 & 28)
 
30.       The Committee is of the view that foreign tourists constitute an important component of tourists who wish to
 visit the Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands.  The restrictions on foreigners to stay beyond permitted period
 in the Islands and visiting only selected islands has discouraged the foreigners from visiting these islands.  The
 Committee, therefore, recommends that in order to optimally exploit the potential of tourism in these islands, the
 restrictions on the foreigners on visiting the islands may be removed and they may be permitted to stay/enjoy the
 beauty of the islands for longer periods.  The Committee also feels that opening up new islands for foreigners also
 needs to be given priority and recommends that the Central Department of Tourism should take up the proposal
 regarding opening up of more islands for the foreign tourists with the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
31.       The Committee appreciates the Government for having opened some areas of Nagaland for foreign tourists and

 is of the view that the levying of U.S. Dollars 30 from the foreigners who wished to visit Sikkim will discourage the
 foreign tourists from visiting Sikkim.  The Committee recommends that the government should consider abolishing the
 permit system for foreign tourists, as has been done in the case of Assam and Meghalaya.  The Committee hopes that it
 will definitely help in boosting foreign tourist arrivals in the state.
 
Reply of the Government
 
32.       The matter has been taken up with the Ministry of Home Affairs regarding the opening of more islands in A&N
 and Lakshadweep and abolishing of permit system as was being done in Assam and Meghalaya.  The Committee ’s
 views on the effecting of the levy of USD 30 from foreigners visting Sikkim has also been communicated.  A reply
 from the Ministry of Home Affairs is awaited and the Standing Committee will be apprised of action taken by the
 Ministry of Home Affairs as soon as their reply is received.

 that it should be expedited at an early date.
 
CONSTRAINT OF COASTAL REGULATION ZONE ACT
RECOMMENDATION (Para 30)
 
34.       The Committee is of the view that the impact of tourism on the environment and ecology requires serious
 consideration.  There is no doubt that unplanned tourism not only degrades the environment physically and otherwise
 but also carries the seeds of its own destruction.  However, the Committee feels that the provisions of CRZ Act do not
 take into account the unique features of the coastal lines of various States in the country, particularly of Andaman &
 Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands and Kerala.  India has many beautiful beaches, which can be developed from
 tourism point of view.  The Committee recommends that the Government should, therefore, seriously consider relaxing
 the provisions of the Costal Regulation Zone Act.  The Ministry of Environment and Forests should also take a liberal
 view and consider positively the proposals seeking relaxation of CRZ restrictions for tourism projects.
 
Reply of the Government
 
35.       Department of Tourism, Government of India has taken up the issue with the Ministry of Environment & Forests
 to relax CRZ Regulations as it poses serious impediment in the development of beach tourism and have suggested that
 the Notification may be modified to enable State Governments to undertake tourism activities.  A recommendation has
 also been made that certain specified areas may be treated as Special Tourism economic Zones.
 
36.       In the case of Andaman & Nicobar Islands the Department of Tourism has proposed to constitute a High
 Powered Committee under the Chairmanship of Minister of Tourism & Culture comprising of the following members
 to discuss, finalise and approve all tourism projects relating to Andaman & Nicobar Islands:

      3.    Secretary(Tourism), Government of India
      4.    Secretary, Ministry of Environment and Forests
      5.    Chief Secretary, Andaman & Nicobar Islands
      6.    Joint Secretary, (NAVY), Ministry of Defence
      7.    Joint Secretary (UT), Ministry of Home Affairs
      8.    Joint Secretary, Department of Tourism             --         Convenor

37.       The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Department of Tourism to constitute a High Powered
 Committee to discuss, finalise and approve all tourism projects relating to A&N Islands and recommends that
 similar action be taken to sort out the problem relating to CRZ regulations.
LACK OF CONNECTIVITY
RECOMMENDATION (Para 32)
 
38.       The Committee feels that there exists a fairly large domestic tourist movement in the country.  However, one
 major stumbling block before the inter-state tourism is poor connectivity.  Domestic Tourism cannot be promoted
 unless the air, rail and road links across the various states and places of tourist interest in the country are improved.  In
 absence of a comfortable access to the places of tourist interest, the tourist cannot be encouraged to visit such places. 
 The Committee, therefore, recommends, that the tourist destinations in the country should be well connected by rail,
 road and air with the urban centres/cities of the region to ensure easy accessibility.  Also the movement of the trains
 should be regularised and speeded up.  The Committee also feels that tourism is closely interlinked with the Civil
 Aviation Sector.  Air linking of the various tourist places in the country as well as places abroad from where tourist
 arrival is expected is essential for development of tourism in the country.  The Committee also recommends that efforts
 should be made to explore the possibility of upgrading the Veer Sarvarkar Airport at Port Blair and Bagdogra Airport
 into international airports so that these places could find a place on the international tourist map.  Also, The Ministries
 of Civil Aviation and Railways should take steps for providing the necessary infrastructure and improve air and rail
 connectivity to the various states in the country.
 
Reply of the Government
 
39.       The matter has been taken up with the Director General Civil Aviation, Ministry of Railway for raising/boosting
 the connectivity in all the tourist destinations.  The Committee has recommended the need of upgrading the Veer
 Sarvarkar Airport at Port Blair and Bagdogra Airport into international airports so that these places could find a place
 on the International Tourists Map and this has also been taken up with the DGCA.  As and when the reply is received
 from the above authorities, the Standing Committee will be apprised of the action taken by the Ministry of Railways/the
 Director General Civil Aviation for increasing tourism connectivity to the tourist destinations as well as upgrading the
 domestic airports to international airports.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
40.       The Committee notes the reply and recommends the Department of Tourism to vigorously pursue the
 matter with the Ministry of Railways and the Director General Civil Aviation for increasing tourism
 connectivity to the tourist destinations as well as upgrading of domestic airports to international airports.

INTRODUCTION
         I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism & Culture,
 having been authorised by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby present this Seventy-third Report of the
 Committee on the Action Taken by the Government on the recommendations/observations contained in its Sixty-sixth
 Report on Demands for Grants (2003-2004) of Department of Tourism.
2.      The Sixty-sixth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and
 Culture was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 10
th April 2003.
 
3.      Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained in its Sixty-sixth Report were received
 from the Department of Tourism on 17th July 2003.
 
4.      The Committee considered the subject and adopted the Report in its meeting held on 29th October 2003.
 
NEW DELHI
October 29, 2003
Kartika 7, 1925 (Saka)                                   
NILOTPAL BASU
 Chairman,
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee
 on Transport, Tourism & Culture.
REPORT
           
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the observations/recommendations as
 contained in its Sixty-sixth Report on Demands for Grants (2003-04) (Demand No. 91) of the Department of Tourism which
 was presented to the Parliament on 10th April 2003.
 
2.         Action Taken Replies have been received from the Government on 17 th July 2003 in respect of all the
 observations/recommendations contained in the Report.  These have been categorized as follows:-
 
(i)                  Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
 
Para Nos. 15, 20, 24 & 29                                                                     Total - 4
 
(ii)                Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the Government replies:
 
Para Nos. 34 & 45                                                                                Total – 2
 
(iii)               Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not been accepted by the
 Committee.
 
      Nil                                                                                                   Total - 0
 
(iv)              Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still awaited:
 
Para Nos. 7, 9, 26, 40, 50, 51, 55, 56 & 59                                               Total - 9
 
3.         The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which have been categorized as
 interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest.
 
4.         On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of the action
 taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry.  The recommendations of the Committee contained in the Sixty-sixth Report, action
 taken thereon by the Government and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of action taken have been
 given in the succeeding paragraphs.
 
THE APPROACH IN THE 10 TH PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 2003-04 (Recommendation at

 paras 7 and 9)
 
5.         The Committee is happy to note that the plan allocation of Rs.225.00 crores of the Department of Tourism was not
 subjected to any reduction at R.E. stage during 2002-2003 and the outlay for the year 2003-2004 has also been hiked
 substantially from Rs.225.00 crores to Rs.325.00 crores.  The Committee hopes that the maximum amount of plan outlay would
 be utilised properly and substantially during the first five months of the current financial year so that the Department will be in
 a position to make demand for more allocation of funds at R.E. stage   for development of tourism infrastructure and promotion
 of tourism in the country.
 
6.         The Committee notes that for the financial year 2002-03, the expenditure upto January 2003 has been only 55% i.e.
 Rs.124.876 crores out of the total plan allocation of Rs.225 crores.  Though, the Department of Tourism have assured that the
 total allocation would be spent by the end of the financial year i.e. 31st March 2003 the Committee however, is unable to
 understand as to how the Department would be able to spend the remaining 45% of the plan allocation within a short span of
 just 2 months of the financial year.  The Committee therefore, disapproves the tendency of spending funds desperately towards
 the end of the financial year. The Committee recommends that the Department should evolve some mechanism of uniform
 utilization pattern through out the year so as to avoid incurring expenditure at the fag end of the financial year.
 
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
7.         The Department of Tourism has formulated schemes of Integrated Development of Tourist Circuits,
 Product/Infrastructure and Destination Development and Assistance for Large Revenue Generating Products during the year
 2002-03, the first year of the Tenth Five Year Plan. Schemes were formulated in consultation with the Planning Commission. 
 Being restructured schemes SFC meetings were called for approval and release of funds.  It took time in finalisation of these
 schemes.  State Governments/UT Administrations were requested to submit detailed projects proposals for these schemes.  As
 the State Governments submitted the proposals after preparing detailed project reports, there was delay in release of funds to
 the State Governments.  But the Department of Tourism utilized the allocated funds of Rs.225 crores during the year 2002-03. 
 In fact the Department of Tourism sought additional grants of Rs.34.50 crores for completion of old projects.  Additional funds
 of Rs.25.00 crores were provided in March 2003 and these were fully utilized.  The recommendation of the Committee will be
 followed by the Department and efforts will be made for uniform utilization of funds during the year 2003-04. 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
8.         The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism has formulated schemes of Integrated Development of
 Tourist Circuits, Product/Infrastructure and Destination Development and Assistance for Large Revenue Generating
 Products during the year 2002-03.  However, the Committee desires that State Governments may be given some
 reasonable time and  requested to submit project proposals for the schemes within that stipulated time limit only for
 avoiding delays in finalisation of project proposals.  The Committee also recommends that old pending projects must
 also be completed by the Department of Tourism and if need be, additional grants may also be provided.
 
INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT OF TOURIST CIRCUITS
(Recommendation at para 15)
 
9.         The Committee is happy to note that Department of Tourism is taking a holistic approach for development of these six
 tourist circuits in the country on each year and providing necessary infrastructural facilities within these circuits and
 convergence of resources in coordination with States/Private sector.  The Committee also notes that Department of Tourism has
 decided that in future funds will not be provided to small isolated projects, which are not of much importance for the
 development of tourism in the country and concentrate on the development of important travel circuits alone.  The Committee
 recommends that more tourist circuits region wise covering more than a State/UT may be selected and developed on the basis
 of the tourism potential of the places according to international standards and aggressive marketing efforts may be taken up in
 order to attract more and more tourists to these places. 
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT

RURAL TOURISM
(Recommendation at para 24)
 
17.        The Rural Tourism is a new market concept to tap tourist traffic as it can form the perfect vehicle for achievement of the
 national objective of achieving partnerships between local communities, government and industry.  Besides, it would help
 generate employment at local level, dispensing with the need of migrations to distant places for earning livelihood thereby
 leading to economic betterment. The Rural Tourism can also provide a solution to the increasing trends of industrialization and
 help in countering the stress of urban life styles and other urbanization syndromes. The Committee feels that global tourism
 growth potential can be harnessed as a strategy for Rural Development and therefore, recommends that the Department of
 Tourism should develop a strong platform around the concept of Rural Tourism for achieving the national objectives in better
 perspective.

04.  Planning Commission has agreed for a provision of 15 crores exclusively for Rural Tourism Projects.

20.        The Committee notes that the efforts being made by the Department of Tourism for development of rural
 tourism in the country during the year 2003-04.  The Committee is of the view that the funds which are being
 earmarked exclusively for Rural Tourism Projects should be utilized properly in order to tap tourist traffic globally.

 cruise vessels. The Committee however, couldn’t understand as to how the scheme has been finalized when the proposals under
 the scheme are yet to be received by the department of tourism. It shows that the Department is lacking pro-active approach in

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
22.        The Department of Tourism formulated the scheme ‘Assistance for Large Revenue Generating Projects’ during the year
 2002-03, the first year of the Tenth Five Year Plan in consultation with the Planning Commission A budget provision of
 Rs.6.00 crore was earmarked for this scheme during 2002-03.  The objective of the scheme is to strengthen tourist infrastructure
 in the country through Public and Private Sector partnership.  During the year 2002-03 the entire budget provision of Rs.6.00
 crores has been spent for the projects under this scheme.
 
23.        The recommendation of the Committee will be followed and the State Governments/UT Administrations have already
 been requested vide Letter dated 24
th April 2003 to submit the project proposals for consideration during the year 2003-04.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
24.        The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism have requested the State Governments/UT Administration
 for submission of project under large revenue generating projects scheme to strengthen tourist infrastructure through
 public and private sector partnership in their respective states and recommends that Department of Tourism should
 keep pursuing the State Governments/UT Administration for timely submission of projects under the scheme.
 
CAPACITY BUILDING FOR SERVICE PROVIDERS
(Recommendation at para 29)
 
25.        The Committee appreciates the scheme launched by the Department of Tourism for training the persons in an
 unorganized sector consisting of small hotel, dhabas and restaurant and other eatable joints spread all over the country
 including tourists guides. The Committee is of the opinion since tourism industry plays a nodal role in displaying the rich
 cultural heritage to the world at large, and possesses high employment potential, personnel engaged in this sector are different
 from those required by personnel engaged in other sectors.  The Committee hopes that this would adequately cater to the
 training needs of the persons engaged in the unorganized sector and helps them is upgrading their quality.  The Committee
 desires that sufficient funds should be allocated under this head and efforts should be made to make the scheme more effective
 by expanding its coverage to the important tourist circuits/tourist destinations.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
26.        The Department of Tourism has formulated the “Guidelines” for the newly launched scheme of “Capacity Building for
 Service Providers” to standardize and also to make the scheme effective.  Under the scheme, training will be provided by
 Institutes of Hotel Management/Food Craft Institutes/Indiatourism Offices and Indian Institute of Tourism & Travel
 Management to the service providers in the unorganized sector.  In order to provide uniformity in the training Department of
 Tourism is formulating model/standard “Training Programme Modules” as well as an “Annual Calendar of Training
 Programmes” for the implementing institutions.
 
27.        During the year 2002-03 the Budget allocation of Rs.150 lakhs under the scheme was fully utilized by providing funds
 to IHMs and Food Craft Institutes.  In the current financial year i.e. 2003-04 there is a provision of Rs.200 lakhs allocated under
 this Head and funds shall be released to Indiatourism Offices and IITTM also, in addition to the IHMs and FCIs.  The
 Department shall follow a monitoring mechanism to review and monitor the training programmes conducted by various
 institutions to make the scheme more effective and uniformly implemented so as to cover the important tourist destinations in
 the country.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE

 training programmes conducted by various institutions to make the scheme more effective and uniformly implemented
 so as to cover the important tourist destinations in the country.  The Committee further recommends that monitoring
 mechanism should be adequately strengthened to ensure quality training.
 
OVERSEAS PROMOTION AND MARKETING
(Recommendation at para 34)
 
29.        The Committee observes that though the allocation for overseas promotion and publicity has been increased
 substantially during the year 2003-04 still there is a significant gap between the Government of India’s spending and the world
 average expenditure on travel and tourism which can not be abridged keeping in view the crunch of financial resources. The
 Committee also notes that Department of Tourism has reoriented itself to the overseas market with a view to changing global
 scenario and fierce competition in the tourism generating markets. The Committee however, recommends that Department of
 Tourism should consider new strategy in the changing patterns of consumer behaviour and adopts integrated marketing
 communication approach to secure the future of the industry and its potentiality for job creations. 
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
30.        The Department of Tourism has noted the above recommendation and also taken into account the present world travel
 trends and changing patterns of consumer behavior while developing its Promotional Plan for the current financial year.  The
 Plan adopts an integrated marketing communications approach and the elements include advertising, sales promotion, public
 relations and direct marketing for positioning India in key markets under the brand name ‘Incredible India’.
 
31.        In the changing world tourism scenario where mass markets are getting fragmented and destinations are shifting away
 from mass marketing to segmented marketing, the Department lays emphasis on use of information technology and Internet as
 this medium has become a catalyst in this paradigm shift.
 
32.        The plan also envisages a centralized advertising campaign to be launched directly from the Headquarters  in various
 key markets.  The Indiatourism Offices overseas through their annual Action Plans would supplement this campaign as well as
 compliment with promotional activities like participation in fairs and exhibitions, organising of seminars and workshops, direct
 mailing, hosting of media personalities and opinion makers under the Hospitality programme, web marketing, dissemination of
 information through the CD-ROMs and brochures etc.  The main objective behind this strategy is to carefully integrate and
 coordinate various communication channels so as to deliver a clear, consistent and compelling message about India’s various
 tourism products under the brand line ‘Incredible India’.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
33.        The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism has developed the promotional plan keeping in view the
 changing global scenario and competition in the tourism generating markets.  The Committee appreciates the
 Department of Tourism for adopting an integrated marketing communications approach, components of which include
 advertising, sales promotion, public relations and direct marketing for positioning India in key markets under the
 brand name ‘Incredible India’ as per its recommendation.  The Committee wishes that it will help augmenting the
 tourism potential and in view of this desires not to pursue the matter further.
 
TOURISM AND ITS IMPACT ON INDIA’S GROSS DOMESTIC PRODUCT
 (Recommendation at para 40)
 
34.        The Committee is of the opinion that domestic tourism has to act as a pillar of our future tourism policy besides as a
 major engine for economic growth of the country and there is a need to provide strong support to this sector in the form of large
 infrastructure.  The Committee is not satisfied with the efforts of the Department of Tourism due to which India’s share of

 newly constituted bodies like National Tourism Advisory Council, Inter-ministerial coordination group etc. should hold
 meetings regularly and Department of Tourism should bring all contentious issues before these bodies in a proactive
 manner.

 coordination with each other for the development of tourists sector in the country as per the recommendation of the

 peak travel months ranging from October to March and especially from major tourism originating destination like North
 America, Western Europe and South East Asia.   The additional seat capacity from the major destinations would provide
 impetus to tourism and have a positive impact on economic development of India.

40.        The Committee is of the opinion that the potential of domestic tourism has grown substantially during the last few years

 be developed soon. For this purpose possibility of getting foreign assistance and Private Sector participation should also be

 public convenience facilities at the important tourist destinations.  This may be done with the involvement of State
 Government/Local bodies/Municipal Corporation. The Committee notes the reply of the Department of Tourism on the
 recommendation of the Committee contained at Para 60 of the 55
th report which says that: -
 
"The recommendation of the Standing Committee and the provision of luggage carrying trolleys at the station,
 which are of tourism importance has been noted by the Ministry of Railways, Railway Board."
 
41.        The Committee is not satisfied with the lackadaisical attitude of the Department of Tourism in taking up the matter with
 Ministry of Railways.   The Committee should be informed about the actual action taken by the Ministry of Railways in this
 regard and in this connection Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation contained in 55th Report, which is reproduced
 below;
 
 “The committee recommends that the Department of Tourism should take up with the Ministry of Railways for

 kind that are available at the airports. These trolleys could be made available to the tourists against payment as in

43.        The Ministry of Railways is running regular Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Janshatabdi Express trains connecting various
 tourists places.  The Railways, however, has welcomed the proposal of running special tourist trains with private sector
 participation subject to operational and financial viability.
 
44.        The Ministry of Railways have noted the recommendation of the Standing Committee regarding the provision of
 alternative methods of carrying baggage at the Railway Stations like trolleys etc. and information of action taken in this regard
 is being collected.

 with private sector for the tourists at different locations in India and a proposal for running special tourist trains with
 private sector participation is under consideration of Ministry of Railways.  However, Committee desires that
