 North-Eastern region of the country to the extent required by them.  The Committee recommends that, in such a
 scenario, keeping in view the socio-economic conditions of the North-Eastern region, the Government must provide
 resources for the projects on its own and the developmental activities in road sector for North-Eastern region should not
 be allowed to be a casualty.
(Paras 62 and 63)
NEED FOR AN INTEGRATED TRANSPORT POLICY
            The Committee observes that one of the objectives for the Tenth Plan for the road sector is ‘Development of
 roads to be considered an integral part of the total transport system supplementing other modes, integrating the
 development plans with railways and other modes of transport’.   This objective of the Tenth Plan reinforces the need to
 have an integrated transport policy in the country.  The Committee is of the view that the modal-mix in terms of
 transport is very adverse in the country inspite of the fact that we have long inland waterways, a fairly large railway
 network and the recent upsurge in the aviation and road transport sector.  However, in absence of the right kind of
 modal-mix the country is not making optimum utilization of all those resources.  There is, therefore, a need to have a
 more balanced and equitable distribution of passenger and freight traffic in the country.  The Committee, therefore,
 recommends that the Government must come forward with an integrated transport policy to make optimum utilization
 of the various transport facilities available in the country.
                                                                                                                        (Para 65)
DAMAGE IN TSUMANI HIT AREAS
            The Committee observes that the Tsunami waves caused extensive damage to the road network and bridges in the
 Southern Parts of the country.  The Committee appreciates the promptness with which the Department of Road
 Transport and Highways responded to the situation and carried out the relief measures in the tsunami hit areas.  The
 Committee strongly recommends that the Department should consider the proposals submitted by the State
 Governments for restoration of the damages on priority basis so that construction/repair works could be carried out at
 the earliest.  The Committee further observes that damage to the National Highways has badly affected the tourism
 potential in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, which is the lifeline of these islands.  The Committee recommends that
 priority should be given to the restoration of the National Highway network and bridges etc. in these islands.
(Para 69)
RESTRICTION ON EXPENDITURE BY MINISTRY OF FINANCE
            The Committee appreciates the concern of the Ministry of Finance for ensuring that the expenditure position in
 all the Ministries should have an even flow throughout the year.  In order to achieve this, Ministry of Finance have
 issued a direction that only 33% of the BE should be spent in the last quarter of the year.  However, so far as
 Department of Road Transport and Highways is concerned, the working in different parts of the country is affected due
 to weather conditions and the restriction imposed by the Ministry of Finance creates a setback to the physical activities
 in the areas of construction of Highways and Bridges by the Department. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
 the Ministry of Finance may reconsider its decision and taking into account the peculiarity of the pattern of utilization of
 funds due to factors which are beyond the control of the Department, the Department of Road Transport and Highways
 should be exempted from any such restriction on expenditure and should be allowed to spend their allocated budget on

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/84threport.htm[28-08-2018 13:07:32]
 various activities which are required to be carried out during that particular period.       
                                                                                                                        (Para 73)
ROAD SAFETY
            Road safety is of paramount importance and undermining it can have disastrous results.  This is evident from the
 fact that the rate of accidents as well as number of fatalities in our country are unusually higher compared to most of the
 other countries.  The Committee notes with concern that there may be a shortfall of Rs.1 to 4 crore in this sector.  The
 Committee is of the view that the Department of Road Transport and Highways, as the agency for distribution of funds
 under this head, has the responsibility to ensure optimum utilization of funds.  The Committee recommends that
 Department of Road Transport and Highways should impress upon the concerned agencies/NGOs the need for early
 completion of formalities and submission of relevant documents so that the funds earmarked for the purpose during a
 particular year are not underutilized.   
                                                                                                                        (Para 80)
POLLUTION TESING AND CONTROL
            The Committee understands the reasons for shortfall in respect of Pollution Testing Equipments during 2004-05. 
 Since revised emission norms have been introduced from 1.10.2004, the Committee recommends that Department of
 Road Transport and Highways should impress upon the State Governments for early procurement of pollution testing
 equipments during 2005-06 so that, if required, the allocation for the purpose could be increased at RE stage.  
            The Committee is of the view that vehicular emission has become one of the major sources of environmental
 pollution and the share of the transport sector in total emissions is a matter of serious concern.  The Committee
 appreciates the steps taken by the Department of Road Transport and Highways in controlling vehicular pollution.  The
 Committee recommends that the Department of Road Transport and Highways should impress upon the State
 Governments the need for effective monitoring and enforcement of these norms for on-road vehicles so as to minimize
 its ill effects.                   
                                                                                                                                       (Paras 83 and 86)
DIFFERENTIAL PRICING SYSTEM FOR PRIVATE VEHICLES
            The Committee expresses its concern that in the absence of user-friendly public transports, the people in the
 country are resorting to excessive use of private vehicles and this has put the roads under undue pressure.  The
 Committee observes that most of the investment on roads is being extracted from the public itself but the returns
 accruing to the users are not equitable. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the efforts of the Government
 should focus on developing public transport, which discourage excessive use of private vehicles.  The Government
 should adopt a methodology, whereby, in the more densely populated states, the rich and the affluent are asked to pay
 more for keeping more than one vehicle. 
(Para 89)
USE OF RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
            The Committee understands that Automotive Research Association of India, Pune has been set up by the Indian
 vehicle and automotive ancillary manufacturers and it is the Department of Road Transport & Highways's authorised
 certification agency for emissions norms etc.  Almost all vehicle manufacturers and major ancillary manufacturers are
 members of this institute.  The Committee is at a loss to understand as to why Government of India's emission norms
 etc. may be certified by an agency which has vehicle manufacturers as its members and on which the Department of
 Road Transport & Highways does not have any administrative control.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that
 either the Department of Road Transport & Highways should have control on the Automotive Research Association of
 India, Pune or the Association should be divested of the power of fixing emission norms as apex certification agency.  It
 is a direct case of the manufacturers themselves being the regulators, which promotes the scope of corruption in the
 functioning of the Institute.  The Committee desires that a proper enquiry may be instituted in the functioning of this
 institute.
            The Committee is constrained to note that the Department of Road Transport & Highways could utilize only
 Rs.7.00 lakh for Research & Development out of the total allocation of Rs.7.9 crore during 2004-05, which makes
 evident as to how much priority the Department of Road Transport & Highways attaches to the Research &
 Development activities.  The Committee is dissatisfied that the Department of Road Transport & Highways has no
 Research & Development mechanism of its own and the Department has to depend upon other organisations for its
 Research & Development activities.  The Committee recommends that Department of Road Transport and Highways
 should develop an institutional mechanism to undertake research and development activities.  The Department should

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA

 also create a regulator of its own with the requisite technical wherewithal for fixing emission norms, product design and
 development etc.  The Committee also recommends that the Research & Development activities should also be used for
 developing technology for creating cost-effective high quality road network such as existing in Malaysia and some other
 countries.
            The Committee observes that development of road data bank and computerized project monitoring system and
 promotion of use of information technology in the highway sector is one of the objectives of the Government in the
 Tenth Plan.  However, it appears that the Government has not achieved much progress in this sector especially the use
 of Information Technology in online  project monitoring system.  The Committee is of the view that Information
 Technology can also be used as an effective tool for monitoring the implementation of the projects undertaken by the
 Department.    They should also make efforts to integrate research and development activities with their monitoring
 system so that proper monitoring could be kept on the projects undertaken by them, which will also help them to keep
 tab on time overrun and cost overrun of such projects.   The Committee also recommends that efforts cited by the
 Department of Road Transport & Highways like creation of Ministry's chair in the area of development of highway
 system at Indian Institutes of Technology and creation of independent testing facilities for bridges on National
 Highways at Central Road Research Institute, New Delhi may be pursued more vigorously and in case of any difficulty,
 parallel institutions may be identified for Research & Development
 activities.                                                                                                                                                             (Paras 95,

 had been stopped completely.  DGBR had also discussed this issue with HE, the Governor of Manipur, Hon’ble Chief
 Minister and Chief Secretary, Government of Manipur.  It had been decided that the Army would clear insurgents by
 carrying out combing operations and thereafter, dedicated Para Military Force would be deployed.  But, so far nothing

 Committee was further informed that the issue of insurgency falls within the purview of Ministry of Home Affairs.

                                                                              R E P O R T
 
India has one of the most ancient civilization and cultural heritage. In the cultural continuum, different communities through their creative expressions and belief pattern contributed

 significantly over centuries which well blended in the mainstream gradually. This unity in diversity is a distinctive characteristic of Indian culture.  Therefore, in a pluralist social mosaic
 culture is the most crucial role-player which gives meaning to our present existence. The role of Culture lies not only in the context of promotion of economic growth but also in relation to
 other objectives of creating an environment that encourages self-expression and exploration on the part of individuals and communities besides support to arts and artists and encouraging
 active participation in cultural expression by people at large, and developing creativity as a social force.
2.         The Ministry of Culture, which was set up in 1985 through the 174 th Amendment of the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961 was part of the Ministry of
 Human Resource Development; later it was transferred to the newly created Ministry of Tourism and Culture. In May 2004 it has been declared as an independent Ministry and is now
 Ministry of Culture. The Ministry is responsible for the promotion, preservation and conservation of the tangible and intangible cultural heritage of the country. It also promotes mutual
 understanding, goodwill and foster closer relations with foreign countries. Preservation of ancient and historic monuments and records, exploration and excavation of archaeological sites
 and remains, maintenance and expansion of libraries and museums of national importance and observance of centenaries and anniversaries of eminent personalities are among its other
 responsibilities. The institutions of the Ministry, which are engaged in promotion, and dissemination of art and culture broadly are the Zonal  Cultural Centers, Center for Cultural Resources
 and Training, and through the Schemes operated Departmentally. The public private participation in the Ministry is done under the aegis of the National Culture Fund.
3.         The programmes undertaken by the Ministry of Culture can broadly be classified as, Activities of North East Region, Archaeology, Museums, Anthropology and Ethnology,
 Archives and Archival Libraries, Tibetan/Buddhist Studies, Libraries, Akademies and National School of Drama, Promotion and Dissemination of Culture, Memorials, Centenaries and
 Anniversaries, Cultural Relations and Festival of India, IGNCA and Secretariat.
4.         Plan programmes of the Ministry of Culture relating to promotion, preservation and conservation of the cultural heritage of the country is implemented through a network of 2
 attached offices, 6 subordinate offices and 26 Autonomous organisations under its control and through 16 schemes directly operated by the Ministry for promotion and dissemination of art
 and culture.  Its activities and programmes have been organized under eleven broad heads. They are Promotion & Dissemination, Archaeology, Museums, Archives, Anthropology,
 Performing Arts, Libraries, Buddhist and Tibetan Institutes, Activities for North Eastern Region and Other Expenditure.

8.         Demand No.20 containing the details of budget allocation of the Ministry of Culture for the financial year 2005-06 was considered by the Department-related Parliamentary Standing
 Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture at its meeting held on the 29
th March 2005.  The Secretary Ministry of Culture during the course of oral evidence held on 29 th March 2005,
 deposed before the Committee :
“This year has been a difficult year for them as the Ministry had major financial constraints.  The budget was passed late and they had accordingly a shorter time to spend the
 money allocated to them.  There was also a cap by the Ministry of Finance.   Accordingly the Ministry of Culture had to spend 65% of the money by December and thereafter
 there was a slash of about Rs.65 crore at the revised budget stage.  After intervention of the Ministry they got restoration of the cut to the extent of Rs.20 crore.  But this has
 certainly put a strain on the institutions/field offices functioning under the Ministry.”
 
9.         The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry of Culture had proposed an outlay of Rs.551.12 crore and also got an approved outlay of the same amount with a capital component
 of Rs.61.80 crore.   The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Culture will be able to utilize the funds for implementation of new Schemes/Projects optimally. 
10.       The Committee, however, is not convinced about the reasons cited by the Ministry that budget was passed late and accordingly, there was shorter time available to spend the money
 allocated to them and observes that if the annual plan starts after the beginning of the financial year itself, then it considerably reduces the capacity of the Ministry to plan out expenditure.  
 Therefore, the planning for financial progress has to start even before as the broad heads are already known to the Ministry under the contours of the five-year plan.  The Committee also
 fails to understand as to how this intra-year financial development should deter the Ministry in planning it in such a manner that none of the financial allocations made can be successfully
 used by the end of the year.  Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that the Finance Ministry recalling the money which has been already allocated is a serious problem and the
 Ministry should take adequate care and evolve a sound method of financial planning so that such kind of circumstance may never occur in future.

 14.      The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) was established in 1861.  It is an attached office of the Ministry of Culture.  Since its establishment, 144 years ago, the ASI has grown into
 a large organization having its network throughout the country.  At present, the ASI has declared 3656 monuments, which are of national importance in the country, including 17 properties
 inscribed on the World Heritage List by UNESCO.  The major activities of the ASI are maintenance, conservation and preservation of centrally protected monuments/sites and remains.  It
 conducts archeological exploration and excavation regularly.  It also keeps developing epigraphical research, setting up and reorganization of site museums and training in archaeology. The
 Archaeological Survey of India has prepared perspective plans for the 10
th Five Year Plan period which envisaged an integrated approach covering conservation, preservation, landscaping,
 organizing/ re-organising of site museums and problem oriented excavations and exploration.   With a holistic approach, the Archaeological Survey of India is devoted towards creation of
 cultural hubs encompassing facilities for domestic and foreign tourists.  The proposed cultural hubs are, i.e. Mahabalipuram, Ajanta & Ellora , Hampi, Kurukshetra, Chittorgarh,
 Kumbhalgarh, Sibsagar monuments and   Fatehpur Sikri.

(iii)       Problem of Encroachment and Security of Monuments/Sites under the Protection of ASI:
 
28.       The Committee was quite concerned about the illegal encroachment of monuments/sites under the protection of ASI and desired to know from the Ministry as to what was being done
 to check the encroachment around the monuments.  The Ministry of Culture replied that as and when an encroachment is noticed in the protected area of a monument, the Superintending
 Archaeologist issues a notice to the encroacher as per the provisions of the Ancient  Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958.  A complaint is also lodged with the local
 police.  When no response is received from the encroacher, the DG, ASI issues a notice ordering the illegal occupant to vacate the occupied site and remove the encroachment.  If no action
 is taken by the encroacher, the DG, ASI issues an order under Section 19 (2) of the Ancient  Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 and Rule 38 (2) of the Ancient
 Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Rules, 1959 to the Collector and the concerned district authorities for demolition and removal of the encroachment.  The Archaeological
 Survey of India also initiates legal action in the courts against the encroachers.  Though the Superintending Archaeologists have been vested with the power of Estate Officer and authorized
 to issue eviction notices under the Public Premises Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants (Act), 1971, the successful removal of encroachment depends upon  entirely on the cooperation of
 the police and district authorities, which is seldom forthcoming.   In the Delhi Circle specifically, there are encroachments on 14 centrally protected monuments and action is under way for
 their removal.  In the case of several encroachments, the matter is sub-judice in the courts of law.  In so far as the Siri Fort Wall is concerned, the protected  stretch of the fortification wall is
 free from encroachment, but a portion of the Siri Fort Wall, which is not under the protection of the Archaeological Survey of India and falling within Shahpur Jat Village, is encroached
 upon by the villagers.   There are two cases in the Court in respect of Siri Fort Wall.
29.       The Director-General, ASI during the course of oral evidence also submitted that  :
"Encroachment in and around ASI monuments is one of the problems ASI is facing.  3,658 monuments are protected.  If you put a reasonable number of people to protect it, it
 would require at least 7-8 thousand people.  If you take monuments like the Taj or Red Fort, each would take at least 200 people.  In fact, it is consuming one-third of the
 staff to protect just these two.  There is no physical protection at all and the encroachment is going on for several years.  We have powers to issue notice for the people to
 vacate.  But we don't have the power to compel them to vacate. This State Government police support hardly ever comes." 
 
30.       The Ministry of Culture informed the Committee that at present, there are 3463 Monument Attendants in Archaeological Survey of India.  CISF personal have been employed in Red
 Fort in Delhi and the Taj Mahal in Agra.  For 459 CISF personnel employed in these two sensitive monuments, the financial implication per year is Rs.9.25 crores.  Besides, 100 State
 Police personnel are being paid for deployment at some monuments and museums.  The total payment involved to the State Police personnel is Rs.1.5 crores annually.  However a large
 number of protected monuments all over the country are not having any security.  There is no precise estimate of the funds required for providing security guards to all these monuments. 
 However on purely tentative estimates, it is estimated that an amount of Rs.100 crores may be required annually for proper physical security to all the protected monuments by way of
 deploying private security guards.
31.       The Committee expresses its anxiety over the incidents of encroachment upon the land of Centrally Protected Monuments.  The Committee is more concerned about the inability of
 Archeological Survey of India to get back the land from encroachers.  Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that a complete assessment should be made regarding encroachment
 of monuments/sites under the protection of Archaeological Survey of India all over the country.  Prompt action ought be taken against the encroachers with the help of State
 Governments/Local Administrations and the matter should be pursued at the highest level.  The Committee also recommends that adequate budgetary provisions should be made for security

 Museum will undertake conservation of Art objects using 3D digitization technology. The Indian Museum will reinitiate plying Museo-Bus or the Museum on wheels which is designed to

37.       Museum Security is a major concern today since a museum is a repository of so many invaluable things which have high market price.  In view of recent thefts at some major
 museums in the country; museum security has become a matter of great concern.  Giving the details of measures taken for the security of museums in the country, the Ministry informed that
 the a Departmental Committee has been constituted to review and suggest improvements in security arrangements.  This internal Committee has so far convened four meetings at New

 besides training of security personnel to operate on these security gadgets, since it is felt that modernization and security are closely inter-related.  The Committee further directs the

NATIONAL ARCHIVES OF INDIA

OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS 
 AT A GLANCE
 
The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry of Culture had proposed an outlay of Rs.551.12 crore and also got an approved outlay of the same amount with a capital component
 of Rs.61.80 crore.   The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Culture will be able to utilize the funds for implementation of new Schemes/Projects optimally. 
            The Committee, however, is not convinced about the reasons cited by the Ministry that budget was passed late and accordingly, there was shorter time available to spend the money
 allocated to them and observes that if the annual plan starts after the beginning of the financial year itself, then it considerably reduces the capacity of the Ministry to plan out expenditure.  
 Therefore, the planning for financial progress has to start even before as the broad heads are already known to the Ministry under the contours of the five-year plan.  The Committee also
 fails to understand as to how this intra-year financial development should deter the Ministry in planning it in such a manner that none of the financial allocations made can be successfully
 used by the end of the year.  Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that the Finance Ministry recalling the money which has been already allocated is a serious problem and the
 Ministry should take adequate care and evolve a sound method of financial planning so that such kind of circumstance may never occur in future.
            The Committee notes that the Ministry of Culture this time has given more emphasis to various reputed institutes of art and culture like, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies,
 Gandhi Smriti and Darshan Samiti, Buddhist and Tibetan Institutes, Multi Purpose Cultural Complexes, Ram Krishna Mission Institute of Culture, Kolkata, etc.  The Committee hopes that
 the construction of proposed new Multi Purpose Cultural Complexes in Manipur, Nagaland, Assam, Rajasthan, Chattisgarh  and Andhra Pradesh would be completed in time.  The
 Committee further directs that the additional amount of Rs.46 crore which has been for the first time provided for Centenaries and Anniversaries Celebration will be spent fairly and in an
 unbiased manner. The Committee also recommends that ongoing projects on publication of volumes of works of Lok Nayak Jaiprakash Narayan be completed in time and funds for that
 purpose will be provided as assured by the Ministry.    Moreover, Birth Anniversary Celebrations of Lok Nayak Jaiprakash Narayan and Choudhary Charan Singh should be continued
 every year.  The Committee strongly recommends that the entire provisions made by the Ministry of Culture be utilised during the year 2005-06.  
(Paras 9, 10 & 13)
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA
The Committee notes that the Plan Allocation for ASI has been increased by Rs.10.00 crore in BE 2005-06.  The Committee hopes that this increased allocation would be utilized on
 those various activities of ASI for which it has been asked for.
(Para 18)
NON-WRITING/PUBLICATION OF EXCAVATION REPORTS
            The Committee is of the opinion that if the excavation reports are not published in time then all the tax payers money spent on them goes waste.  The Committee is utterly dissatisfied
 that despite repeated recommendations made earlier by this Committee, the Ministry is still not in a position to indicate specific time frame by when this job will be accomplished.  The
 Committee observes that the labour and the money gone into excavations undertaken by the Archaeological Survey of India for the knowledge to crystallize for generations and the efforts

MERGER OF NATIONAL MISSION ON ANTIQUITIES AND NATIONAL MISSION ON BUILT HERITAGE
 
In view of the explanation given by the Ministry the Committee concludes that the whole process indicates confusion in the decision making process and complete lack of
 farsightedness on the part of the Ministry in planning its programmes and projects which has not only affected the rich cultural heritage of the country but also led to valuable wastage of
 time and resources. 
            The Committee fails to understand that why so much additional work was given to the ASI when ASI was not able to successfully complete the work already assigned.  The
 Committee is also not convinced about the objectives of these Mission modes.  On the one hand the Ministry has stated that they are not recruiting more staff.  On the other hand the
 Committee has been informed that for the Mission purpose the Ministry will be contractualising jobs on short term basis.  In view of this the Committee directs that the Ministry should
 adopt a clear cut guideline in this regard and the ASI should be provided with appropriate wherewithal so that laudable goals of these Missions do not remain unachieved.
(Paras 26 & 27)
 
PROBLEM OF ENCROACHMENT AND SECURITY OF MONUMENTS/SITES UNDER THE PROTECTION OF ASI
 
            The Committee expresses its anxiety over the incidents of encroachment upon the land of Centrally Protected Monuments .  The Committee is more concerned about the inability of
 Archeological Survey of India to get back the land from encroachers.  Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that a complete assessment should be made regarding encroachment
 of monuments/sites under the protection of Archaeological Survey of India all over the country.  Prompt action ought be taken against the encroachers with the help of State
 Governments/Local Administrations and the matter should be pursued at the highest level.  The Committee also recommends that adequate budgetary provisions should be made for security
 arrangements and protection of monuments, as this is the most crucial aspect of preserving our cultural heritage and wherever possible modern gadgets like, electronic surveillance cameras
 should be installed in the monuments.  The Committee feels that security is a sovereign function.  Hence, it is the responsibility of Central Government to get the monuments and other
 important assets protected.  In view of this, the Committee is of the opinion that the Union Home Ministry should pay the bills towards the expenses incurred for paying the Central Security
 Agencies under this head.  Accordingly, the Ministry of Culture should pursue the matter at the highest level. 
(Para 31)
DISPLAY OF ANTIQUITIES AT SITES MUSEUMS
            The Committee observes that shortage of trained manpower is the reason behind non-displaying of objects found during excavations at various site museums. Therefore, the
 Committee recommends that the ASI should have trained personnel in this field and adequate financial allocation should also be made for the purpose.
(Para 33)
 
NATIONAL MESUEM AND MESUEM SECURITY
The Committee expresses its concern towards the prevailing scenario of museum security all over the country especially, the National  Museum.  It is a matter of urgent need to have
 full proof security to guard the invaluable antiquities preserved at museums.  The Committee, therefore, recommends to acquire modern security gadgets to strengthen the museum security
 besides training of security personnel to operate on these security gadgets, since it is felt that modernization and security are closely inter-related.  The Committee further directs the
 Ministry to provide museums with adequate funds to strengthen their security and to appoint a consultant to solicit global expertise as this is a very specialized subject.  
(Para 38)
NATIONAL ARCHIVES OF INDIA
            The Committee expresses its dissatisfaction over the fact that the post of Director in National Archieves was lying vacant for quite sometime and it was filled up by an acting Director
 on temporary basis.  The Committee does not comprehend the reason for laxity shown by the Ministry in running such an apex institution without any head of the service and the Committee
 recommends that it should be filled up by a regular Director immediately.
            The Committee also hopes that the additional funds allocated during 2005-06 for expansion of record management programme, expansion of Repair and Reprography, construction
 of functional building of NAI, Record Centre at Bhubaneshwar and completion of work of Record Centre, Jaipur will be completed in time.   The Committee should be apprised of the
 progress in this regard.

 Raza Library and Khuda Baksh Oriental Public Library would be done in a time bound manner. The Committee emphasises that in order to keep pace with the latest development in
 information technology all our public libraries should have latest technology and computer networking should be done in a planned manner.

TONNAGE TAX
 
28.       The Government has announced introduction of Tonnage Tax from the financial year 2004-05 for the Shipping Industry with an option for the shipping companies to opt for either
 tonnage tax or corporate tax. This will facilitate investment in shipping sector. The silent features
of the tonnage tax regime are:-
Ø      The introduction of Tonnage tax will provide a level playing field to the Indian Shipping    Industry with its international counterparts.
 
Ø      This will be implemented from the current financial year. 
Ø      At least 20% of the book profits of the companies opting for tonnage tax scheme to be    transferred to a separate reserve to be utilized for acquisition of vessels within 8 years. This
 will help to add more tonnage to the Indian Shipping industry.
 
Ø      Provision regarding mandatory minimum training requirements for the companies opting for the proposed Tonnage Tax regime. 
 
Ø      The shipping companies are to opt either of Tonnage Tax or Corporation tax.
 
Ø      An option for tonnage tax has to be exercised by the company once. The Tonnage Tax regime would remain applicable for 10 years, for the companies opting for the same. 
 
29.       Dredgers have also been included in the Tonnage Tax regime from 2005-06. The Government has been making constant efforts for creating hospitable investment environment for
 the Shipping Industry.  Some of the efforts made/steps taken are as under:
Ø                              Prior to introduction of Tonnage tax, the Indian Shipping Industry were enjoying the benefits under Section 33AC of IT Act. Under Section 33AC shipping
 companies were allowed to create reserves upto twice the paid up capital and reserves including share premium account, which they were supposed to be utilized in next 8 years
 for acquisition of vessels. The amounts so transferred in the reserve were exempted from corporate tax;
 
Ø
                              Import of all types of ships has been included in the Open General Licence (OGL) thereby dispensing with licence requirement for import of various kind of
 ships, as per guidelines issued by the Ministry of Shipping on 15th June,2001 and 5th March,2002 ;
 
Ø                              100 percent Foreign Direct Investment  (FDI) is allowed in Shipping sector;

 written reply stated that while presenting the Finance bill for 2005-06, the Finance Minister has pronounced extension of tonnage tax regime for dredgers only.  However, for vessels
 registered under Indian Vessels Act 1917 and Indian Coastal Vessels Act, 1838 the benefit of tonnage tax has not been extended in this bill.  The issue is being taken up with Ministry of
 Finance for extending the benefits to these types of vessels also.
           
31.       The Committee notes that the Government has since introduced the tonnage tax regime to the dredgers also as per its recommendation.  The Committee feels that introduction of

SETHUSAMUDRAM SHIP CHANNEL PROJECT
32.       India does not have a continuous navigable route around the peninsula within her own territorial waters due to presence of a reef called Adam's Bridge at Pamban near
 Rameshwaram.  Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project envisages cutting of a ship channel to connect the Gulf of Mannar to Bay of Bengal through Palk Bay so that most of the ships,
 depending on the draft required, moving between east and west coast of India could have a continuous navigable sea route around the Peninsula within India's own territorial waters.  This
 will save upto 424 nautical miles of travel and upto about 30 hours of sailing time for ships between east and west coast.    The project will serve the strategic and national security
 interests of the country since the channel can also be used by Naval and Coast Guard ships.  The project is also expected to spur overall economic development of coastal districts of
 Tamilnadu through development of infrastructure, ancillary industries etc. 
33.       To a specific query regarding adverse environmental effects of the proposed channel, the Department of Shipping in its written reply stated that a section of environmentalists have
 expressed their concerns about the potential adverse effects of the proposed channel on environment.  The main apprehensions expressed are:
(a)                Environmental Impact such as effect on marine flora and fauna, oil spillage, increased salinity in waterbed etc.
(b)               Economic Impact such as loss of livelihood of fishermen due to reduction in fish catches.

CRUISE SHIPPING
37.       Cruise shipping is a fast growing sector globally. As a departure from concept of cargo and passenger ships, cruise is like a moving township studded with all state of art facilities
 including all types of recreational activities. The idea is fast catching, because, journey on a cruise is not only pleasurable, but also almost free from sea travel health hazards. Experience
 gained in the Caribbean, Latin American and South-East Asian countries indicates that huge amount of foreign exchange can be earned by providing the right policy environment and
 infrastructure for the growth of cruise shipping. India with its vast and beautiful coastline, virgin forests and undisturbed idyllic islands, long historical and cultural tradition of
 architecture, theatre and performing arts can prove to be fabulous destination for cruise-tourists.  The global scenario for cruise shipping is picking up very fast, with an annual increment
 from 10-20% in the cruise ship fleet and passengers carried. Further, Indian coastline is unfortunately not witnessing the same growth pattern as mentioned.  Therefore, it is said that a
 strong policy intervention by the Government of India would be necessary for its stimulated growth. 
 
38.       To a specific question regarding efforts for growth of cruise shipping in India, the Department of Shipping in its written reply submitted that in order to formulate cruise shipping
 policy a High Power Steering Group under the Chairmanship of Minister of Shipping, Road Transport & Highways and Union Minister of State for Tourism (Independent Charge) as Co-
Chairperson has been set up on 29.9.2004.  The first meeting of this Group was held on 14
th December 2004 in which the draft Concept and Policy Paper for Cruise Shipping in India was
 discussed at length.  Various issues concerning this sector have been taken up and Working Groups have been formed to tackle all the issues.  Three Working Groups have already
 finalized their reports, which will come up before the Steering Group for providing finality to their recommendations.  Other Groups are also progressing well and it is hoped that very
 soon their recommendations will be compiled and given a final shape to the proposed policy.  The draft policy paper has also been deliberated by the Consultative Committee of this
 Ministry in its Meeting held on 20.12.2004.  A Workshop was also convened at Mumbai on 12.2.2005 which was attended by Members of the Consultative Committee, various
 stakeholders, hospitality industry, shipping lines, cruise lines, tour operators and shipping agents.  Once a policy is in place, besides providing a direction to the growth of cruise shipping,
 it will also remove the bottlenecks pertaining to the sector.
39.       The Committee desired to know the details of private sector participation for development of infrastructure and other facilities at various ports, the Department of Shipping in its
 written reply informed that working group comprising of the representatives of Department of Tourism, the major ports and the industry was constituted by Department of Shipping for

 Mangalore, Cochin, Tuticorin and Chennai be selected for the development of infrastructure and other facilities so as to make India as an attractive cruise destination.  In the second phase,

 Board has a total of 6623 pensioners as on 28.2.2005 and the Board is at present paying only the pensionary benefits (without pension relief w.e.f 1.1.2002) to 1761 pensioners, while the
 balance 4862 pensioners are drawing pension at the pre-revised rate only.  To meet the monthly liability of full pension as on 28.2.2005 to the existing 6623 pensioners, the Board would
 require around Rs.2.30 crores per month. To meet the outstanding liability of 6623 pensioners, the Board would require Rs.67.33 crore as on 28.2.2005.  In addition, there are outstanding
 liabilities on account of D.A. arrears, encashment of leave, medical reimbursement, LTC, PLR etc. amounting to Rs.9.02 crores.  Thus, the total outstanding dues of Calcutta Dock
 Labour Board as on 28.2.2005 is Rs.76.35 cores. 
 
45.       Though there has been improvement in the performance of the Board in the last 2 years, it may be difficult to sustain this performance for long because, the manpower of CDLB is
 depleting at a very fast rate and the bulk of its workers will retire in another 2 years.  Hence, it will be impossible for the Board to sustain its present level of activity by 2007-08 because
 of non-availability of work force. It is already becoming increasingly difficult for the Board to supply gangs satisfactorily and it would not be possible to meet the requirement at the port

49.       The Committee is distressed to note that the employees of the Calcutta Dock Labour Board are not being treated as Government employees so far as payment of pension and
 pensionary benefits are concerned, though, the Calcutta Dock Labour Board, a body corporate, was constituted in terms of section 5(A) of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment)
 Act, 1948 in September 1952.  The Committee expresses its concern that inspite of specific provisions under the Act, the rules and regulations concerning pension for employees of
 Calcutta Dock Labour Board have not been approved by Department of Expenditure and the employees of Calcutta Dock Labour Board are being made victims under the cover that
 Calcutta Dock Labour Board constitutes an autonomous body and therefore, denied of the benefits for long.
 
50.       The Committee is of the firm opinion that liabilities on account of payment of arrears of pensions and pensionary dues of Calcutta Dock Labour Board entirely lies on the
 Government and the Government cannot be absolved of its liability and withhold pension and post retirement benefits to the employees of Calcutta Dock Labour Board on one pretext or
 other.  The Committee, strongly recommends, the Department of Shipping to vigorously pursue the matter with Ministry of Finance for release of enhanced grant to Calcutta Dock Labour
 Board for meeting its pensionary liabilities and implement comprehensive restructuring of Calcutta Dock Labour Board for introduction of Voluntary Retirement Scheme.
 
51.       The Committee is of the view that problem for payment of pension and pensionary dues can be resolved once and for all, if the Government approves self-sustaining proposal for

 Committee, therefore reiterates, that the Government should build a corpus of pension fund for discharging the future pensionary liabilities of the Board, as the bulk of its employees will
 retire in another two years.

 members in the event of death of seamen members.  This was a contributory Provident Fund and the employees were required to deposit the Provident Fund contributions in respect of
 Seamen employed by them with their watching contribution with Seamen's Provident Fund Organisation after the terminations of each voyage.  The prevailing rate of contribution was 12

INDIAN INSTITUTE OF MARITIME STUDIES(IIMS)
57.       In order to make appropriate changes in the institutional frame work and financial arrangements for imparting maritime training with the active participation of the Industry and
 keeping in view the need to augment maritime training facilities, including the feasibility and desirability of bringing the institutes under a university type of structure, the Government of
 India in October 1991 set up a committee on Maritime Education & Training (COMET).  The committee in its report submitted in May 1992, recommended establishment of an autonomous
 apex body named as Indian Maritime University to manage, control, supervise, direct and monitor the Maritime Training Institutions functioning under the Government control.  
 Accordingly Indian Institute of Maritime Studies (IIMS) was registered as a Society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 on 6 th June 2002 and as a Charitable Trust under Bombay
 Public Trusts Act, 1950 on 15 th January 2003.  The four Maritime Training Institutions, namely (1) Lal Bahadur Sashtri College of Advanced Maritime Studies and Research, Mumbai, (2)
 T.S. Chanakya, Navi Mumbai, (3) Marine Engineering and Research Institute, Kolkata and (4) Marine Engineering and Research Institute, Mumbai have been placed within the domain of
 Indian Institute of Maritime Studies.
 
58.       As regards, establishment of Indian Maritime  University under an Act of Parliament, the Department of Shipping in its written reply informed the Committee that an Expert
 Committee including representatives of University Grants Commission has been constituted to look into the feasibility of formation of Indian Maritime  University (IMU). The
 Committee held several meetings and visited training institutes at Mumbai and Kolkata and recommended for the formation of Indian Maritime University by an Act of Parliament
 under the aegis of Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways, Department of Shipping. As a consequence to this a draft Indian Maritime University Bill has been prepared.
 
59.       To the specific querry regarding fixing time limit for the establishment of Indian Maritime University, the Department of Shipping stated that the financial implications are
 being worked out. It is expected that the Indian Maritime University may probably come into existence during 2005-06. Keeping this in view, a token provision of Rs.1.00 crore on the
 Plan side has been made during the financial year 2005-06 for development of Indian Maritime University.

 Committee on Accommodation has been sent to Cabinet Secretariat on 7.2.2005 for consideration. As regards, creation of pension fund and finalization of terms and conditions for the
 absorption of employees of Indian Institute of Marine Studies, it is stated that till the employees are on deemed deputation to Indian Institute of Maritime Studies and absorbed therein,
 they continue to be Government servants. Thus, creation of pension fund and settling of terms and conditions appears to be premature at this stage. Moreover, in the wake of
 establishment of Indian Maritime University under a Central Act will automatically take care of all these issues, without any disadvantage to the employees.

" … I do not think I am in a position to give a final reply.  It is true that it is now a maritime university and which has to be a new institution it can be set up only after the

 scales.  So, that has nothing to do with Indian Institute of Maritime Studies or university that has been going on for a period of more than ten years because Government has

INLAND WATER TRANSPORT
 92.      Inland Water Transport (IWT) is an efficient mode of transport from the point of view of energy consumption, cost of transportation of environment friendliness. IWAI executes
 various Schemes for development of the Inland Water Transport infrastructure namely fairway development, terminals, and navigational aids for National Waterways.  So far, following
 three waterways have been declared as national waterways:-
National Waterway No.1 (NW-1)
            Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system from Allahabad to Haldia (1620 kms) - declared as national waterway in 1986.
National Waterway No.2 (NW-2)
            The Brahmaputra river from Sadiya to Dhubri (891 kms) - declared as national waterway in 1988.
National Waterway No.3 (NW-3)
            The west coast canal from Kollam to Kottapuram alongwith Champakara and Udyogmandal canais (205 kms) - declared as national waterway in 1993.

(i)         Kakinada-Pondicherry canal along with rivers Godavari and Krishna
(ii)        The river Barak, and
(iii)       East Coast Canal along with river Brahmani and Mahanadi delta

OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS
AT A GLANCE
 
ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2005-06
            The Committee expresses its concern over the failure of Department of Shipping to spend the approved outlay.  During the year 2004-05, out of the budgeted amount of Rs.2419.66
 crore the Department could spent only Rs.1400.99 crore which clearly indicates the poor fiscal management in the Department of Shipping.  The Committee observes that even while
 revising allocations, little consideration has been paid to the actual expenditure incurred in the past.  This shows that budgetary and revised estimates have always been made without
 taking into account the actual requirements as experienced in the previous years.
           
The Committee feels that Department of Shipping has not evolved effective system or planning to systematically anticipate, assess and project its actual requirements of funds
 otherwise the investments could have yielded commensurate returns.  The Committee recommends that in future, the Department of Shipping should be transparent and realistic while
 making projections of required funds so that resources may not remain unused and are allocated more judiciously.

PORT SECTOR
The Committee is unhappy with the poor performance of Department of Shipping with regard to under utilization of approved outlays over the years for the port sector.  During the
 Financial year 2004-05, an outlay of Rs.1066.55 crore was allocated for the port sector but the ports could utilize only Rs.440.51 crore. The Committee is dismayed by this repeated failure
 of Department of Shipping and is surprised as to why the Ministry asks for so much of allocation if it is not in position to spend the approved outlay. The Committee desires that the
 Department of Shipping should take all corrective measures based upon actual requirements for maximum utilization of budgeted amount during 2005-06.  In this regard, the Committee
 reiterates its earlier recommendation contained in 81st report of Demands for Grants (2004-05) of Ministry of Shipping which reads as under:-
"The Committee fails to understand as to how the physical targets will be achieved with this low utilization pattern.  In fact, the Committee feels that this raises doubts about
 the mismatch in the projections for physical and financial targets.  The Committee is of the view that the Ministry of Shipping has full responsibility to ensure proper
 utilization of the approved outlay.  The Committee feels that strict monitoring is crucial for timely completion of any project.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that
 the monitoring agency should play rather proactive role and do away with the procedural hurdles for timely completion of the projects so that the budgeted allocation is
 utilized optimally.  The Committee also recommends the Ministry to keep informed about the progress in the matter."
            (Para 16)
CAPACITY AND TRAFFIC IN MAJOR PORT
            The Committee expresses its appreciation for achievement of the capacity of major ports which has either exceeded the target or likely to achieve target fixed for cargo handling of
 all commodities except container.  The containerization is the emerging global trend in the mode of cargo trade in which the country is lagging behind which is a matter of concern.
           
The Committee feels that a proper environment with transparent procedures and decision making process can give boost to private sector participation in the port sector.  The
 Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to review the existing guidelines on Private Sector Participation in the port sector with emphasis on overcoming capital
 constraints, technology upgradation and value addition.
(Paras 26 & 27)
TONNAGE TAX
            The Committee notes that the Government has since introduced the tonnage tax regime to the dredgers also as per its recommendation.  The Committee feels that introduction of
 tonnage tax in lieu of corporate tax will not only facilitate investment in shipping sector but also provide a level playing field to the Indian Shipping Industry vis-à-vis its foreign
 counterparts and the shipping companies will be able to acquire more tonnage.  However, the Committee is unable to comprehend the reasons for excluding the vessels registered under
 the Indian Vessels Act 1917 and Indian coastal vessel Act, 1838.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the matter for extending the benefits of tonnage tax to the vessels registered
 under Indian Vessels Act 1917 and Indian Coastal Vessels Act, 1838 may be pursued further with the Ministry of Finance as this also vitally linked to the viability of the Inland Water
 Transport sector.
(Para 31)
SETHUSAMUDRAM SHIP CHANNEL PROJECT
            The Committee notes the Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project is of great economic and strategic importance which will connect the Gulf of Mannar to Bay of Bengal so that the
 ship moving between East and West coast of India could have a continuous navigable sea route within their own territorial waters and the proposed channel save upto 424 nautical miles of
 travel and about 30 hours of sailing time for ships.  The Committee notes with satisfaction that Ministry of Environment & Forests has also given environmental clearance to the project
 and a special purpose vehicle has been incorporated to raise finance to create and operate navigable channel.  The Committee expects that the project once completed will serve the
 strategic and national security interests besides spuring the overall economic development of coastal districts of southern states.  The Committee however, recommends that while taking
 up the implementation of the project, the Department of Shipping must give due attention to the likely effect of natural calamities particularly one like as Tsunami which hit southern
 states during December 2004 and safety measures may be incorporated accordingly.
  (Para 36)
CRUISE SHIPPING
            The Committee is of the view that sea travel is becoming increasingly popular and there is enormous potential for its growth and expansion in India.  The Committee notes that six
 major ports- Mumbai, Mormugao, New Mangalore, Kochi, Tuticorin and Chennai have been identified for the development of infrastructure and other facilities with a view to make India
 an attractive cruise destination.  The Committee notes that a High Power Steering Group has been set up with a view to catalyze the growth and development of cruise shipping and to
 remove bottlenecks and a policy is being formulated in the regard. The Committee hopes that the group will submit its report expeditiously and the policy is framed at the earliest so that
 the benefit of opportunity available to cruise tourism sector is exploited.  The Committee recommends that pending finalization of policy, the Department of Shipping must take steps to
 attract investments from private sector with a view to create infrastructure and other facilities for development of cruise shipping especially in ports on the Eastern parts of the country
 including Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshdweep Islands having great potential in that area.
(Para 40)
CALCUTTA  DOCK LABOUR BOARD
            The Committee is distressed to note that the employees of the Calcutta Dock Labour Board are not being treated as Government employees so far as payment of pension and
 pensionary benefits are concerned, though, the Calcutta Dock Labour Board, a body corporate, was constituted in terms of section 5(A) of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment)
 Act, 1948 in September 1952.  The Committee expresses its concern that inspite of specific provisions under the Act, the rules and regulations concerning pension for employees of
 Calcutta Dock Labour Board have not been approved by Department of Expenditure and the employees of Calcutta Dock Labour Board are being made victims under the cover that
 Calcutta Dock Labour Board constitutes an autonomous body and therefore, denied of the benefits for long.

            The Committee is deeply concerned that the shortage to the tune of Rs.92.78 crore in Seamen's Provident Fund, which lost due to security scam, has not yet been recouped by the

 ship-repair turnover.  The vigorous marketing efforts are showing results  and Hindustan Shipyard Limited has been able to secure the hi-tech, hi-value repair orders for betterment of the
 financial health of the yard.  The Committee appreciates the decision of the Government for rehabilitation of Hindustan Shipyard Limited by way of financial restructuring for improving
 the performance of the yard and recommends for expeditious clearance of the proposal for the capital restructuring of the Hindustan Shipyard Limited.                                     
(Para 76)
HOOGHLY DOCK & PORT ENGINEERS LIMITED
            The Committee is happy to note that a rehabilitation-cum-revival package has been prepared for Hooghly Dock & Port Engineers Limited and a token provision has also been kept
 for the purpose as per its recommendation.  The Committee is of the opinion that Hooghly Dock & Port Engineers Limited with its infrastructure and a expertise can be a integral part for
 development and promotion of Inland Water Transport through NW-1 and NW-2 and contribute to the national economy as well. The Committee, therefore recommends the Government
 to grant clearance for the revival package of Hooghly Dock & Port Engineers Limited expeditiously.
(Para 82)
CENTRAL INLAND WATER TRANSPORT CORPORATION
The Committee notes with distress that the matter for disinvestments of Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd has been referred to the Board for Reconstruction of Public
 Sector Enterprises.  The Committee feels that the Government has not made much efforts to improve the financial health of the company.  The Committee is gravely concern by the fact
 that inspite of repeated recommendation in the past the Government has not yet been able to come out with a complete blueprint for making full use of the existing assets of the company
 in ensuring productive potential by exploring all possibilities like merger with similar entities and integration with Inland Water Transport. The Committee is firmly of the view that the
 future of Inland Water Transport operations including that of Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd holds immense possibilities for establishing a well-defined multimodal
 transportation network in the country and therefore recommends the Department of Shipping to take steps to improve the performance of the Central Inland Water Transport Corporation
 Ltd besides impressing upon the Ministry of Finance for capital restructuring with its existing infrastructure, capacity and manpower.
(Para 91)
INLAND WATER TRANSPORT

REPORT
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/86threport.htm[28-08-2018 13:09:34]
            The Committee is constrained to note that Inland Water Transport has been the most neglected sector and has not been developed with desired pace inspite of its economic potential
 and merely accounts for 0.15% of cargo movement in the country.  The Committee observes that though measures to boost the growth of cargo traffic have been put in place and
 department is committed to raise the share of Inland Water Transport to 2% over the next 8-20 years. The Committee however, notes that with a view to compete with the other developed
 modes of transport, the Department of Shipping is working on declaration and development of three more waterways as National Waterways and a task force to monitor the progress of
 Inland Water Transport projects has also been formed. The Committee, recommends the Department of Shipping to exploit the full potential of this efficient mode of transport, besides,
 addressing the issues of development of adequate infrastructure facilities namely fairways, terminal and navigational aids on the existing three NWs.
 
            The Committee also recommends the Government to improve the modal-mix of transport in the country and prepare a road map for integrated transport policy to include   Inland
 Water Transport, Coastal Shipping, Civil Aviation, Road Transport & Highways and Railways.
            The Committee is perturbed to note the practice of under utilization of budgeted amount by the Department of Shipping over the years.  During 2004-05, the Department of
 Shipping has projected Rs.133.50 crore plan outlays for Inland Water Transport sector, which was reduced to Rs.121.03 at R.E. stage, and ultimately the Department of Shipping has spent
 only Rs.80.00 crore during 2004-05.  The Committee observes that actual expenditure incurred has always been low compared to the budget estimates for Inland Water Transport sector
 including North-East Pool of fund.  The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to intensify its monitoring mechanism to ensure that the budgeted amounts
 earmarked at the B.E. stage are fully utilized during 2005-06.  At the same time the Committee desires that the Department of Shipping should review all the on-going schemes and if
 required, re-allocate the funds budgeted during the financial year.
 
            The Committee notes that a comprehensive Inland Water Transport policy has been announced by the Government to encourage investment from the Private-Public participation
 for accelerated development of Inland Water Transport sector.  The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Department of Shipping for creating transparent, hospitable and conducive
 environment for ensuring both the Private and Public sector participation in the development of Inland Water Transport sector.  The Committee expects that primarily public investment in
 Inland Water Transport sector will definitely help to create infrastructure facilities and augment Inland Water Transport fleet.  The Committee recommends that all pending Inland Water
 Transport specific projects should be cleared expeditiously.
           
The Committee notes with dismay that Research & Development Studies facilities especially in design of vessels and night navigation facilities and identification of economically
 viable routes for development of Inland Water Transport sector has not been given due consideration.  The Committee is of the view that Research & Development activities is the
 backbone for success of any sector and recommends the Department of Shipping to strengthen the Research & Development facilities for development of Inland Water Transport Sector in
 the country.
           
The Committee is happy to note that Department of Shipping has appointed a consultant for working out a realistic target for cargo transportation vis-à-vis targeted investments for
 Inland Water Transport promotion for the 10
th Plan and beyond as per its recommendation.  The Committee hopes that the study for linking the investment in Inland Water Transport
 sector with achievement of physical targets for cargo transportation will certainly enhance the prospects of Inland Water Transport and help to boost the growth of cargo traffic in Inland
 Water Transport sector. The Committee directs the Department of Shipping to apprise it about the progress in the matter.

4.         The approach in the 10th Plan aims to stimulate investment and encourage the State Governments to develop unique tourism products. 
The State Governments would use Tourism as a means for achieving their socio-economic objectives and catalyze the private sector to enhance
investment in tourism.  It seeks to enhance the employment potential within the tourism sector as well as to foster economic integration through
developing linkages with other sectors.  The 10
th

promotion of national integration, international understanding and the earning of foreign exchange besides recognising vast employment
generating potential of Tourism and furthering the socio-economic objectives of the Plan. It also seeks to provide legislative and regulatory

in the promotion of all rich areas of tourism viz., rural, heritage, adventure and eco-tourism.  It focuses on the development of competitive high
quality products and destinations besides addressing the concerns of growth through resolution of contradictions in policy so as to achieve
inter-sectoral convergence of activities that helps to foster the growth of tourism.

The Committee notes that with an aim to improve the existing destinations and circuits and to develop new destinations and

Development of Destinations and Circuits.  However, the Committee is surprised to note that the tourism potential and uniqueness of
some of the important States like Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Tamilnadu, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and  Uttranchal for convergence of

The Committee recommends that more Circuits and Destinations  region-wise should be identified in consultation with the State

benchmarking, the related Ministries and Department of State Governments should have sub-plans in their annual plans so that
tourism related infrastructure projects receive the highest priority.
            The Committee also recommends that purposeful domestic and international publicity and marketing support should also be
provided to all important tourist Circuits and Destinations so as to create interest of the tourists in the Indian tourism products besides
promoting 
India
 as a major tourists destination.

th

 infrastructure instead of spreading it very thinly in small isolated projects.  The

            The Committee observes that Rural Tourism is an important way in addressing the impact of increasing trends of
industrialization and helps in moderating the stress of urban life styles and other syndromes and Ministry of Tourism is paying
adequate attention to the development of rural infrastructure in the country in participation with Private Sector with a view to
translate the structural changes into benefits at the grassroots level.  In this regard, the Committee reiterates its earlier
recommendation contained in 79
th
 Report on Demand for Grants 2004-05 of Ministry of Tourism which may be read as under:-

The Committee is of the view that Rural Tourism has great potential and prospects in the country as it helps to revive the
local peoples' interests and pride in their culture, tradition and values besides generating the tourists interest in the customs of
the indigenous people as it focuses directly on the local people.  The Committee feels that with a growing interest in the
intangible culture of different countries (i.e. lifestyle, cuisine, ceremonies, music, religion, beliefs, customs and history)
,
 there is
an enormous potential to encourage global tourism in rural areas. The Committee recommends the Ministry to develop some
institutional mechanism for supporting, promoting and organizing large number of fairs & festivals and handicrafts & craft
melas/bazaars in rural areas which will provide exposure, recognition as well as, additional flow of income to local artisans.  The
Committee further recommends that the Ministry should actively coordinate its efforts for liaising with other

opportunity than any other industry in the country
